sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: The R endorsement for personal-use rental or recreational rigs hauling household goods starts past twenty-six thousand pounds or forty feet for Class D and E drivers, needs form MV-forty-four and a permit fee covering at most two road tests, a road test in matching size and type with no written test beside a supervisor twenty-one or older licensed for the rig, about fifteen minutes of turns, intersections and curb backing, then an office visit and fee.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: Which two measurements trigger the R endorsement, and how does its testing path differ from a regular license?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: The R endorsement trips on either bulk or length, past twenty-six thousand pounds or forty feet, and its road test has no written companion, unlike the ordinary license path.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: Which form starts a first-time New York license, what steps follow, and how are first-license expiration and fees set?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: First-timers file form MV-forty-four at any office or from the DMV website, pass vision and knowledge tests plus fees, and mostly finish a five-hour pre-licensing course and road test; the first license runs at most five years to the birth month and day with Class D, DJ, M and MJ fees set by age and birth date.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: How many name-proof points must an applicant reach, what signature rule applies, and when is a New York photo card worth all six?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: Applicants supply a Social Security number plus English name and age proofs from the point lists on forms MV-forty-four point one, MV-forty-four.1RID, ID-forty-four and ID-44RID; name proofs must total six points with one signed, and a current New York photo card alone is worth six points unless expired over two years.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: How do form MV-forty-four, the six-point signed-document tally, and a current New York photo card fit together at check-in?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: Form MV-forty-four opens the application, but the six-point identity tally with one signed paper is a separate gate, and a current New York photo card alone clears all six points.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: Which parent or agency statements, passports, consular IDs, and out-of-state or foreign photo licenses carry four identity points?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: Four-point proofs are DMV statements MV-forty-five for applicants under twenty-one, MV-45A for government-represented applicants, and MV-45B for homeless youth unusable for Enhanced or REAL ID; a valid United States passport or card; an English foreign passport with visa and entry proof or embassy-certified translation; a consular identity document; a photo foreign license; and a photo card from another United States jurisdiction or Canadian province, current or expired at most two years.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: Which immigration, citizenship, military, benefit, and border-crossing photo documents count for three identity points?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: Three-point papers are a valid re-entry permit, refugee travel document, citizenship or naturalization certificate, unexpired resident card, valid photo work-authorization card, military photo card for active, reserve or retired members, photo benefit card, and border-crossing card.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: Which school ID pairs, vehicle papers, military dependent cards, and Social Security cards earn two identity points?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: Two-point papers include a military dependent card, non-photo interim license or computer permit, title, registration, Social Security card, high-school photo ID with report card or transcript, and college photo ID with transcript.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: Which vital-status records, permits, tribal or benefit cards, and recently expired immigration cards also earn two points?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: More two-point papers are a government marriage, divorce or name-change record, professional license, pistol permit, tribal photo card, foreign-government marriage, divorce or name-change record, benefit card without photo, foreign school record with photo, and resident or work-authorization cards expired at most two years.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: Which banking, employment, insurance, utility, school-diploma, and tax items count for one identity point each?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: One-point papers are a major credit card, ATM card with preprinted name and signature, canceled check with preprinted name, bank record, employee ID, pay stub showing the name, check-cashing card with preprinted name and signature, life policy in force two years, health or prescription card, utility bill with name and address, diploma or equivalency, and a W-two showing the Social Security number.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: Which remaining cards or tax records earn one point, and which six official documents separately prove date of birth?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.memory_hook: Birth certificate or passport proves age
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: The list ends with a union card, veteran access photo card, court document naming the applicant, foreign school record without photo, municipal photo ID, tax transcript or taxpayer-number letter, and Social Security statement; age is proved by one government birth certificate, state or city birth-registration certificate, military photo ID, United States passport, foreign passport with immigration papers, or citizenship or naturalization certificate.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: What visual acuity must an applicant reach in at least one eye, and where are failures or special-lens cases routed?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: Vision needs twenty-forty in at least one eye with or without correction, and failures or special lenses go to a DMV call center.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: Which four subjects appear on the twenty-question written test, and what overall and road-sign minimums are required to pass?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: The Class D, M, DJ, MJ and E written test spans road rules, safe driving, signs, and alcohol and drug law, passing at fourteen of twenty including two of four sign items, with the manual's items and website quizzes as practice.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: Why would scoring seventeen out of twenty still fail the New York permit test if you missed three sign questions?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: The written test has twin bars, fourteen of twenty overall and two of four signs, so strong rules knowledge still fails without the sign minimum.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: Which extra manuals cover motorcycles and CDLs, and at what age can students take the high-school OKTA online knowledge pre-test?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: Motorcycle applicants also study manual MV-21MC and commercial applicants manual CDL-ten for a separate test; Class D tests run multilingual on touch screens or paper; students from fifteen years eleven months may pre-test through OKTA at participating high schools in English or Spanish with instant on-screen scoring, and schools need no driver-ed program, just a connected computer, printer and monitor.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: How do the twenty-forty eye check, the written exam, and the high-school OKTA pre-test line up as separate steps?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: Vision screening at twenty-forty and the written test are independent gates, and the OKTA online pre-test only works for students from fifteen years eleven months at participating schools.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: Once a student passes or fails the school online test, what happens next for office application or retakes?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: Online passers take a receipt, instructions and forms to any office from age sixteen to apply, and failures retake online as often as the school allows.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: How do New York junior driving rules define properly licensed, guardian, in loco parentis, and a qualifying school course?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: Properly licensed means licensed in-state for the driven vehicle; a guardian is a court-appointed durable stand-in parent; in loco parentis is a consented parent-role stand-in; a school course is state-approved instruction or Armed Forces training excluding zero-credit activities.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: What daytime hours, supervisor rules, dual-brake requirements, and nighttime rules govern junior permits in New York City and Long Island?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: Junior-permit days run five morning to nine evening under a parent, guardian, in-loco-parentis adult, teacher or instructor with dual-control brakes in the city, the same list or a written designee on Long Island, while both regions ban night driving outright.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: Who may supervise an upstate junior permit holder from five morning to nine evening versus after nine evening?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: Upstate junior-permit days accept any supervisor twenty-one or older with a valid license, and upstate nights return to the five-person supervisor list.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: How do New York's three regions compare on nighttime and daytime junior-permit practice?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: Junior-permit nights ban city and Long Island driving outright yet allow supervised upstate driving, while days everywhere demand a qualified supervisor, tighter in the city and on Long Island than upstate.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: How are work, work-study, medical, and daycare trips defined, and which specific bridges, parks, test zones, and Westchester parkways ban learner permits?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.expected_back: Employment is scheduled paid work excluding driving as the job, work-study is an approved program such as credit-bearing BOCES courses, medical trips cover needed household care, and daycare trips enable family work or study; permit holders always carry a twenty-one-or-older supervisor licensed for the vehicle, a parent, guardian or instructor in the city and on Long Island, and avoid test areas, city park streets, Triborough crossings, and the Cross County, Hutchinson River, Saw Mill River and Taconic parkways.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: What baseline rule applies to every learner-permit supervisor statewide, and how do downstate rules tighten it?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: The supervisor must be twenty-one or older and licensed for the vehicle everywhere, but the city and Long Island further require a parent, guardian or instructor, unlike upstate.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: What passenger cap, belt and child-seat duty, and front-seat rule apply whenever a junior-permit holder drives?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: Junior-permit drivers take at most one under-twenty-one passenger unless immediate family or a qualifying supervisor rides along, belt every occupant with child restraints, seat only the supervisor up front, and face added junior sanctions in the next chapter.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: How many total, after-sunset, and heavy-traffic practice hours should candidates build, and what course is required before scheduling a road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: Test candidates should log fifty hours with fifteen after sunset and ten in heavier traffic, rehearse expressways beyond city streets, prefer school-based lessons, and finish an approved safe-driving course, automatic in driver education or as pre-licensing with an adult online pilot, before booking.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.front: How long does a five-hour pre-licensing certificate stay valid, and does the defensive point-and-insurance course substitute for it?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.expected_back: In-person course graduates present the certificate, valid one year, at booking, and the point-and-insurance crash-prevention course does not satisfy the requirement.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.front: How many points and what percentage of insurance rates can New York's crash-prevention course trim, and how often can it repeat?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.expected_back: The certified crash-prevention course, sold privately in class or online as point-and-insurance reduction, erases up to four points when eligible, repeats every eighteen months, and cuts liability and collision base rates ten percent for three years.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.front: What benefits does the Point and Insurance Reduction Program deliver, and why do permit holders still need a separate pre-licensing course?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.expected_back: The DMV-certified Point and Insurance Reduction Program can reduce eligible driving-record points and lower base liability and collision insurance rates, but it does not satisfy the Safe Driving Course requirement.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.front: What are the exact point, month, percentage, and year numbers for PIRP, and how does it relate to the Safe Driving Course?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.expected_back: When eligible, the Point and Insurance Reduction Program reduces up to four points from your driving record every eighteen months and qualifies you for at least a ten percent reduction in base liability and collision insurance premiums for three years, without meeting the Safe Driving Course requirement.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.front: How long must a junior permit stay valid before testing, what three papers come to the road test, and how do seventeen-year-olds upgrade?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.expected_back: Juniors upgrade by filing the MV-two hundred eighty-five student certificate and surrendering the junior license, or hand the permit to the examiner for automatic upgrade, else limits run to eighteen; the permit must hold valid six months first, and test day needs MV-two hundred seventy-eight or MV-two hundred eighty-five on file, the photo permit, and a parental MV-two hundred sixty-two certifying fifty hours with fifteen after sunset.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: How do the fifty-hour practice breakdown and the six-month valid-permit rule compare before a junior road test?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: Before the road test, DMV states you should have at least fifty hours of practice—including at least fifteen after sunset and a recommended ten in moderate to heavy traffic—whereas a junior learner permit must be held in valid status for at least six months before taking the road test.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.front: What must every test vehicle and accompanying driver meet at arrival, and what extra vehicle must a motorcycle candidate provide?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.expected_back: Test cars must be registered, inspected, insured, equipped and roadworthy with a clean free examiner belt, arriving drivers bring a twenty-one-or-older licensed supervisor, and motorcycle applicants supply a car, truck and driver for the examiner; other permit holders show photo permit plus MV-two hundred seventy-eight or MV-two hundred eighty-five on file, booking online or at one-five hundred eighteen-four hundred two-two thousand one hundred.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.front: What separate purpose does each road-test form serve across MV-two hundred seventy-eight, MV-two hundred eighty-five, and MV-two hundred sixty-two?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.expected_back: MV-two hundred seventy-eight proves the five-hour course, MV-two hundred eighty-five proves student driver education, and MV-two hundred sixty-two certifies supervised hours, three papers with three distinct jobs at test time.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.front: How do you drive legally right after passing your New York road test while waiting about two weeks for the mailed card?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.expected_back: Schedulers keep the MV-two hundred seventy-eight or MV-two hundred eighty-five proof ready, weather can cancel tests with online notices, and after the drive the examiner explains result delivery while an online interim license carried beside the permit covers driving until the photo card mails in about two weeks.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.front: What non-family young-passenger cap, seat-belt duty, and regional restrictions still bind teens after passing the road test onto Class DJ?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.expected_back: Junior-license holders take at most one non-family under-twenty-one passenger, belt all occupants with child restraints, face added sanctions in the next chapter, and follow Class DJ regional place, time and company limits.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.front: Which exact employment or enrollment documents must a junior licensee carry for solo job, farm, or school travel on Long Island and upstate?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.expected_back: Solo Nassau and Suffolk job runs, farm work included, need MV-58A employment proof, or upstate a dated signed employer letter naming business, driver, duties, schedule and a verification contact; solo school or work-study runs need a dated signed letterhead enrollment letter with official contact, activity schedule and places, and driver identity.

sec01-card-sec01-R15.front: How does a junior driver's solo destination determine whether to carry form MV-58A, an employer letter, or school letterhead?
sec01-card-sec01-R15.expected_back: Solo job runs need MV-58A employment proof, or upstate an employer letter, while solo school runs need a letterhead enrollment letter, so the destination picks the paper.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.front: Where and when may a Class DJ junior license holder drive solo during daytime and nighttime across NYC, Long Island, and upstate?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.memory_hook: Free days outside NYC, restricted nights
sec01-card-sec01-F36.expected_back: Licensed-junior days allow city solo runs only straight between home and job, work-study, college, evening high school, driver education or farm work, or accompanied by a qualifying adult, with free daytime driving on Long Island and upstate; nights ban city driving, limit Long Island solos to school and farm shuttles, and limit upstate solos to job or school runs with other night driving adult-accompanied.

sec01-card-sec01-R14.front: How do after-nine-evening rules for a Class DJ license split across New York City, Long Island, and upstate?
sec01-card-sec01-R14.memory_hook: City zero, Island school-farm, upstate work-school
sec01-card-sec01-R14.expected_back: Licensed-junior nights ban the city, shuttle school and farm trips on Long Island, and allow job or school runs upstate, a three-way split that mirrors but never matches the permit chart.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.front: What passenger and quarter-mile supervision rules govern learner-permit and junior motorcycle or moped riders?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.expected_back: Permit and junior motorcycle and moped riders carry no passenger but the supervisor, who holds the same-class license, stays within a quarter mile in general control, and should keep the rider visible.

sec01-card-sec01-R16.front: Who is the only permissible passenger on a Class M or MJ permit or junior license, and how close must supervision stay?
sec01-card-sec01-R16.expected_back: A Class M or MJ motorcycle or moped learner permit or junior license allows no passenger except a supervising driver licensed for the same class, who must maintain general supervision and control within one quarter mile and should ideally keep the rider in sight.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.front: How fast must you report a New York address change, what do you write on your card, and how early can you renew?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.memory_hook: Report moves ten days, ink back
sec01-card-sec01-F38.expected_back: New York permits and junior licenses work elsewhere only where allowed under local limits, so visitors check with local authorities; address changes reach the DMV within ten days by mail, form MV-two hundred thirty-two or web with the new address inked on the license back; drivers track expiry, notices mail forty-five days ahead, missing notices mean an office visit, and renewal runs one year early.

sec01-card-sec01-F40.front: How can active-duty service members extend a New York license, and what deadline binds newly settled residents?
sec01-card-sec01-F40.memory_hook: Duty plus six months, thirty-day resident
sec01-card-sec01-F40.expected_back: Service members keep their license through active duty plus six months after discharge on sixty-day MV-seventy-five notice; out-of-state and foreign licensees drive until residence, then apply within thirty days.

sec01-card-sec01-F41.front: How do transfer steps differ between US or Canadian newcomers and other-country newcomers, including keeping a foreign card from destruction?
sec01-card-sec01-F41.expected_back: New residents surrender United States or Canadian licenses with added identity proof plus vision, adding written, road and course work for short-held or long-expired licenses; other-country newcomers pass vision, course, surrender, written and road steps with the foreign card destroyed unless a written hold is filed and returned only after surrendering the New York card; young visitors obey both states' limits and nobody under sixteen drives.

sec01-card-sec01-R17.front: How does New York summarize newcomer testing by origin alongside the rules for young out-of-state visitors?
sec01-card-sec01-R17.expected_back: United States and Canadian newcomers surrender and test lightly, other-country newcomers test fully, young visitors obey both states, and nobody under sixteen drives at all.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: Who must yield when you approach an intersection on a fresh green light while another driver is still mid-intersection turning left?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: Approaching drivers yield to traffic already inside, so a green-straight driver waits out a left turner mid-intersection before entering.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: When opposite-direction drivers arrive together, who holds priority, and how should a left-turning driver stage and keep their wheels while waiting?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: Simultaneous opposite arrivals give straight and right movements priority over left turns, with left turners entering on green only when nobody ahead also turns left, holding right of center with straight wheels, finishing when oncoming clears, yielding the same way into driveways and lots, and waiting out any doubtful gap.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: At an uncontrolled crossroads or when two right-angle vehicles stop at the exact same moment, which driver yields?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: At uncontrolled or simultaneous-stop right-angle corners, the left driver yields to the right driver, even going straight against straight.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: How do opposite-arrival left turns and simultaneous right-angle stops both place the yielding duty on leftness?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: Left turns bow to straight and right traffic while simultaneous-stop corners make the left driver bow to the right, so leftness loses in both geometries for different reasons.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: What stop, yield, and directional-looking rules apply when pulling out of a New York driveway, parking lot, or private road?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: Driveway, lot and private-road exits must stop and yield to roadway traffic and pedestrians, watching left for right exits, both ways for left exits, and any crossing pedestrian.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: How does your legal duty exiting a private driveway contrast with entering an intersection on a green signal?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: Driveway exits stop for everything while green lights still stop for nobody except whoever is already inside, entry caution versus earned passage.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: How must New York drivers treat pedestrians and cyclists at painted or unmarked crosswalks, including stragglers after the light turns green?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: Drivers yield to lawful crosswalk pedestrians marked or not, slowing or stopping as needed and guarding cyclists too, waiting out red-light pedestrians after green and crosswalk users on either side before turning.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: When must you hold back behind the line even though your traffic signal shows steady green?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: Never enter on a green you cannot clear, waiting out backed-up far sides and offset cross-streets instead of gridlocking the box.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: Who holds the right-of-way when your vehicle approaches a New York traffic circle or rotary?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: Motorists entering a traffic circle or rotary must give way to vehicles already circulating inside, while detailed roundabout navigation appears in Chapter Eight.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: How must every direction respond to approaching fire, ambulance, or police vehicles flashing red combinations, even without a siren?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: Fire, ambulance, police and authorized emergency responders showing red, red-blue or red-white flashes with possible sirens or air-horns, which police may skip, command an immediate safe pull to the right edge and stop from every direction, after clearing any intersection, including opposite-lane two-way approaches and sirens of unknown location.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: Which ordinary traffic rules may authorized emergency drivers break when running lights and sirens, and why must you stay alert?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: Lit-and-sounding emergency drivers may legally speed, run reds and stop or yield signs, reverse one-way streets and invent turning moves, so nearby drivers stay extra cautious despite the responder's duty of care.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: What speed and lane actions does New York's Move Over law require past stopped emergency, hazard, or shoulder-parked highway vehicles?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: The Move Over law demands care, reduced speed and, on multilane parkways, interstates and controlled roads, a lane shift away from shoulder-stopped emergency and hazard vehicles flashing emergency, amber or blue-green lights unless unsafe, plus blue-green-light vehicles and any shoulder-parked vehicle on parkways and controlled highways, all punishable as a moving violation.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: Which volunteer or service drivers use solo blue, green, or amber lights in New York, and are they authorized emergency vehicles?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: Volunteer firefighters show blue, volunteer ambulance crews green, and plows, tow rigs, tow-blue combos, rural mail carriers and school buses amber, yet none count as authorized emergency vehicles, their drivers obey every law, and others yield only by courtesy.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: Compare your legal obligations across red-flashing emergency rigs, solo blue-green-amber courtesy lights, and shoulder-stopped highway vehicles?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: Authorized emergency vehicles flashing red, red-and-blue, or red-and-white lights require pulling safely to the right edge and stopping, whereas vehicles displaying only blue, green, or amber lights receive courtesy yielding, and the Move Over law requires slowing—and changing lanes when safe on multilane controlled-access roads—for stopped lit emergency or hazard vehicles and for any stopped motor vehicle on a parkway or controlled-access highway.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: At least how many feet ahead must you signal every turn or lane change in New York, and should you signal before braking?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: Every turn and lane change needs lamp or hand signals at least one hundred feet ahead, preferably before braking, with illustrated hand shapes on the page.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: Why must turn prep double-check for motorcycles, keep front wheels straight, mind rear-wheel tracking, and scan low beside right curbs?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: Turn preparation slows down, scans all sides with motorcycle paranoia since unseen bikes cause most car-bike crashes, holds wheels straight until committed, tracks the tighter rear-wheel path, and guards pedestrians, cyclists, moped riders and low-hidden wheelchair, stroller and suitcase users, especially turning right.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: How close to the right edge should you approach and finish a standard right turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: Right turns hug the right edge without sweeping wide and land in the entered road's right lane unless signs say otherwise.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: Which lane do you start from and land in when turning left from a one-way street onto another multi-lane one-way street?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: One-way-to-one-way lefts stage in the left lane and land in the entered road's left lane where two exist.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: How do you position your car when turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: One-way-to-two-way lefts stage left and enter right of center hugging the line, watching left-road traffic and hard-to-judge motorcycles.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: Where do you stage, pass inside the intersection, and land when turning left from one two-way street onto another?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: Two-way-to-two-way lefts stage in the right half near center, favor the intersection's left side to clear opposing left turners, enter right of center hugging the line, and watch oncoming, cross-lane and easily-missed motorcycle traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: Where do you stage, turn relative to the intersection center, and land when turning left from a two-way road onto a one-way road?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: Two-way-to-one-way lefts stage in the right half near center, cut before the intersection's middle, and land in the entered left lane.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: Which lane must you enter first when turning left from a two-way road onto a four-lane highway, and how do you move right afterward?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: Two-way-to-four-lane lefts stage in the right half near center, enter the left lane right of center, and drift outward when traffic allows.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: What single staging rule unites all five New York left turns, and how do two-way versus one-way landings split?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: Every left stages near its own center yet lands differently, hugging the entered center on two-way arrivals and the left lane on one-way arrivals, one staging rule with two landing rules.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: What safer turnaround beats a highway U-turn, and which lane position and arrow rule govern legal U-turns?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: U-turns reverse direction, belong in lots and driveways with forward re-entry rather than on highways, start only from the leftmost pavement near the centerline never the right lane, and need green-arrow permission with yielding where allowed.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: List the five places or sight-distance limits where U-turns are illegal in New York, and what maneuver replaces them on narrow streets?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: U-turns are illegal where other drivers cannot see your vehicle from five hundred feet in either direction, in New York City business districts, at NO U-TURN signs, on limited-access expressways even where paths connect the sides, and in school zones, whereas a three-point turn may be used on a narrow two-way street unless prohibited and may be required on your road test.
