sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: When do renewal reminders mail out, which three problems block them, and does a missing reminder excuse driving expired?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: Renewals run every two years with mailed reminders forty-five to sixty days out, lost when addresses lapse, three-plus parking tickets stand unanswered, or credentials are suspended, plus two weeks of processing that the owner must anticipate without excuse.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: What happens if your registration expiration date lands on a Saturday, Sunday, or state holiday?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: Expiries landing on weekends or state holidays stretch automatically to midnight of the next business day with insurance maintained throughout.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: How do mail renewals handle alternate shipping, full address updates, carrier changes, Utica mailings, and legal name changes?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: Mail renewal files MV-eighty-two with a separate note for alternate mailing, since addresses written on MV-eighty-two join the record while MV-two hundred thirty-two alone changes every record, plus a check to the Commissioner with MV-204A fee lookup and an insurance card when carriers changed, sent to the Utica processing center with two weeks of patience, longer overseas, and name changes demand an office visit with identity proofs.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: Which vehicles and unchanged account conditions qualify for three-step online registration renewal?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: Online renewal fits unchanged addresses and carriers on passenger cars, small trucks and non-exclusive-off-road motorcycles, showing fees on screen for three-step credit-card renewal mailed within two weeks.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: If a spouse or friend renews your registration in person, whose signature and which IDs must they bring?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: In-person renewal files MV-eighty-two with the registrant's signature, and second parties including spouses must show original identification for themselves plus original or copy for the registrant.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: What key rule distinguishes renewing a registration by mail, online, or at a DMV office?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: Mail renewal tolerates address changes with a side note, online renewal forbids any address or carrier change, and office visits demand the registrant's own signature even through a proxy.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: Must a registered New York vehicle keep liability coverage while sitting parked in a garage or driveway?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: A registered vehicle must stay liability-insured whether driven or parked.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: What are New York's minimum per-crash liability dollar amounts for death, bodily injury, and property damage?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: Minimum coverage is fifty thousand for one death and one hundred thousand for two or more, twenty-five thousand for one injury and fifty thousand for two or more, and ten thousand for property, all per incident.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: What clean ratio links New York's bodily-injury minimums to its fatality minimums?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: Death minimums run fifty and one hundred thousand while injury runs twenty-five and fifty with ten for property, so death always doubles injury at each headcount.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: What happens if insurance drops before turning in car plates, when does your driver license suspend too, and which vehicle is exempt?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: Before coverage lapses, plates go back with an FS-6T receipt or daily civil penalties or registration suspension follow, ninety uninsured days without returned plates suspend the license too, DMV insurance letters demand answers, and motorcycles skip the plate turn-in.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: How does New York treat motorcycles differently from cars when seasonal insurance coverage ends?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: Motorcycles must carry insurance like cars yet skip the plate turn-in on lapse, the chapter's cleanest exception to a universal rule.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: Who must prove valid insurance on New York roads, and what license penalty hits uninsured driving, lending, or crashing?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: Everyone driving or lending a car in the state, resident or not, must prove acceptable insurance, and uninsured driving, lending or crashing revokes at least one year.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: What inspection deadlines apply to New York dealer buys, private buys, and newcomers holding an out-of-state sticker?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: In-state-sold vehicles need inspection within thirty days with a certificate before delivery, non-dealer buys need it within ten days of registration with a VS-one thousand seventy-seven extension on request, and a mover's existing certificate survives to expiry or one year, whichever first.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: How do the thirty-day, ten-day, and up-to-one-year inspection rules match up across vehicle owners?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: Dealer-bought cars enjoy thirty inspection days while private buys get ten after registration, and movers keep an old certificate up to a year, three clocks for three buyer kinds.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.front: Which six special transfers skip a dealer's pre-delivery retail inspection requirement?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.expected_back: Retail inspection exemptions cover welfare-to-work transfers, chassis transfers, factory-direct delivery, out-of-state or country registration, scrap, and lease buyouts.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.front: Which two events require a fresh vehicle inspection, and what color signs mark licensed stations?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.expected_back: Re-inspection falls due before the current certificate expires and on every registrant change, at yellow-and-black official stations, with heavy trucks, buses, tractors and trailers at heavy-vehicle stations and motorcycles at motorcycle stations.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.front: What does your registration-renewal signature certify about inspections, and what happens upon passing versus failing?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.expected_back: Signing a renewal certifies the inspection is current, owners track the annual date and book early for repair time, passers earn a windshield sticker while failures get a rejection notice demanding repair and retest.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.front: What repair spend unlocks an emissions waiver, and which gas vehicles take safety-only inspections?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.expected_back: Failed high-enhanced or OBD II emissions inspections can waive after a genuine repair attempt costing at least four hundred fifty dollars; most gasoline cars take emissions with safety except motorcycles, and cars twenty-six-plus or under-two model years old plus historic registrations take safety only.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.front: What roadside checks apply to any diesel in New York, and what weight rating adds diesel emissions testing?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.expected_back: Diesels running in the state face random roadside safety checks even when registered elsewhere, and ratings over eighty-five hundred pounds add a diesel emissions inspection.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.front: What steps should you follow for a repair or dealer dispute, and what ninety-day or mileage deadline governs repair complaints?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.expected_back: The DMV licenses dealers, stations and repair shops, so buyers verify credentials, complain to management first, then call weekdays eight-thirty to four-fifteen or write the Albany consumer box, with repair complaints due within ninety days or three thousand miles, whichever first.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: Which shapes and color pairs distinguish regulation, warning, destination, and motorist-service road signs?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: Sign shape and color announce their job: regulation signs are normally white rectangles with black or red markings, warnings yellow diamonds with black, destinations green with white, and services blue with white.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: What must you do at a red-and-white stop sign, and in what three-step order do you pick your exact stopping spot?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: The red-and-white stop sign demands a full stop with right-of-way yielded, halting before the stop line, else the crosswalk, else the nearest point with a clear view into the intersection.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: How must you approach a red-and-white yield sign, and when does it turn into a full stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: The red-and-white yield sign demands slowing, traffic checks and readiness to stop, a full stop whenever conditions require, and yielded right-of-way.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: How does a mandatory stop sign differ from a yield sign, including the three-part stopping-point rule?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: A stop sign requires a full stop every time before yielding right-of-way—stopping before the stop line, else the crosswalk, else the nearest point with a view of cross traffic—whereas a yield sign requires slowing down, checking traffic, yielding right-of-way, and stopping fully only when traffic conditions require it.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: Which six traffic rules do white rectangular regulation signs cover, and what does a red circle with a diagonal slash mean?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: Other regulation signs rule direction, lanes, turns, speed, parking and special cases, with a red circle-and-slash banning the pictured action or vehicle and rectangular white signs flagging special rules.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: What do yellow-and-black warning signs alert you to, and what does an attached yellow-and-black speed plaque recommend?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: Yellow-and-black warnings mark hazards and special rules, sometimes paired with a yellow-and-black advisory speed urging slower travel.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: What do orange-and-black road signs signify, how low can work-zone limits drop, and how must you treat flaggers?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: Orange-and-black work signs mark active work with possible flag control and work limits as low as twenty-five, and drivers slow through every work zone and obey every flag signal with or without a posted limit.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: How does the legal force of yellow warning plaques compare with orange work-zone signs and flaggers?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: Yellow warnings advise caution with advisory speeds while orange work signs command slowdowns with enforceable limits and flag obedience, advice versus orders.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: What information do green-and-white guide signs provide, and how do shaped route markers help navigation?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: Green-and-white destination signs give direction and distance, while varied route markers name interstate, United States, state or county roads by shape, in sample order state, United States, interstate, for map planning and en-route tracking.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: Which four traveler needs do blue-and-white highway signs direct you toward?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: Blue-and-white service signs point to rest areas, fuel, camping and medical help.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: In what vertical or horizontal order are traffic-signal colors arranged, and how must you treat a dark or broken signal?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: Signals normally stack red, yellow and green top-to-bottom or left-to-right, appearing lone, flashing, round or arrowed, and dead or broken signals force a stop-sign stop followed by right-of-way rules unless an officer directs otherwise.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: Which two turns on steady red are normally allowed after stopping, and which signs, city rules, or school-bus rules ban them?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: Steady red means stop until green, or arrow-only movement on a green arrow when clear; right on red and one-way-to-one-way left on red are allowed after a full stop with yielding, except where signs, signals or markings forbid, anywhere unposted in the city, and right on red never for a school bus carrying students.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: How does a flashing red light differ from a steady red arrow when you want to proceed or turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: Flashing red equals a stop sign with stop, yield and safe-go, while a red arrow bans all movement its way until it clears, including any turn on red.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: How do turning permissions differ across a standard steady red, a steady red arrow, and an unposted New York City red?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: Steady red allows right turns and one-way-to-one-way lefts after stopping, a red arrow allows nothing, and city reds allow nothing unposted, three reds with three answers.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: What distinct actions do a steady yellow circle, a flashing yellow light, and a steady yellow arrow require?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: Steady yellow warns of imminent red with stopping preparation, flashing yellow orders caution, and a yellow arrow ends green-arrow protection with stopping preparation for intending turners.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: How do flashing red and flashing yellow contrast, and how does a yellow arrow narrow a steady yellow's warning?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: Flashing red copies the stop sign while flashing yellow only urges caution, and steady yellow warns of red while a yellow arrow ends protected turning.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: Does a steady green circle or green arrow give unconditional priority, or must you still yield?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: Steady green and green arrows both permit movement while still yielding right-of-way as the law requires.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: What does each of the four reversible overhead lane-control signals—steady red X, steady yellow X, flashing yellow X, and green arrow—command?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: Overhead lane lights ban the lane on a steady red X, order exit on a steady yellow X, restrict to left turns on a flashing yellow X, and open the lane on a green arrow.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: What traffic rules does pavement paint enforce, when may you cross a solid edge line, and what does an inward-angling edge line warn of?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: Road paint divides lanes, gates passing and lane changes, assigns turn lanes and stop points; edge lines mark the shoulder boundary that crossing breaks except by official order or sign, and an inward-angling edge line warns of narrowing.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: How do white and yellow lane lines differ in traffic direction, and what does a single broken line permit?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: White divides same-direction lanes and yellow divides opposing flows in solid or broken pairs, and one broken line allows passing or lane changes when safe and non-interfering.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: When a solid line and a broken line run side by side, what rules apply to drivers on each side?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: Beside a solid-and-broken pair, the solid side bans passing and crossing except for a left into a driveway, while the broken side passes when safe and non-interfering.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: How do double solid lines differ from a single solid line for passing, lane changes, left turns, and obstructions?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: Double solid lines ban passing, lane changes and crossing except to turn left entering or leaving the road or to U-turn, while a single solid line allows passing and changes only when obstructions or traffic force it.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: How do broken, paired solid-broken, single solid, and double solid lines compare on passing and crossing?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: Broken center lines invite passing, solid-and-broken splits permission by side, double solid forbids everything but lefts, and single solid allows only forced moves, a four-step strictness ladder.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: When must you halt behind painted stop or crosswalk lines, and why are some stop lines painted far back from corners?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: Signed or signaled intersections may paint a white stop line or parallel crosswalk lines, stopping falls before whichever exists only when a device, officer or yielding pedestrian, skater or scooter user demands it, and set-back single lines shelter truck turning room.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: Does rolling up to an empty painted stop bar or crosswalk on a green or unsigned street force a stop?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: Stop lines and crosswalks trigger stops only when a device, officer or yielding user demands, so bare paint alone never forces a halt.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: What do painted pavement arrows require, and by what point must you finish picking your lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: Lane arrows dictate lane use, such as right-only from the right lane and straight-only from the left, with lane choice settled before the solid separator.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: Which vehicles may travel in diamond-marked lanes during posted hours, and when may solo city drivers enter one?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: Diamond lanes reserve for buses, high-occupancy vehicles, bicycles and posted specials during posted times, with city broken-white gaps admitting non-carpool right turns at the next corner, all to speed the highest-value traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: How do human traffic directions rank against lights and signs, and which five authorized roles must you obey?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: Officer directions beat every sign, signal and marking, including stop-on-green and go-on-red orders, from police, fire police, work flaggers, crossing persons and school bus drivers.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: Which two exceptions allow general cars into a diamond lane—by pavement design or by human authority?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: Diamond lanes exclude general traffic except posted compliers and corner-turning entrants, while officer orders override every marking including the diamonds themselves.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: What behavior links a dark dead traffic light to a flashing red light, and what still outranks both?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: Dead signals degrade to stop-sign behavior with right-of-way rules, the same fallback a flashing red gives, while officers can override both.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: How does a license suspension differ from a revocation in New York, and can unlicensed or out-of-state drivers face both?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: Suspension takes the license away for a time before return, possibly with a termination fee, while revocation cancels it outright so reapplication, possibly denied, starts over after the revocation term; the same fates apply to out-of-state driving privileges and to unlicensed permission.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: What violations trigger a sixty-day junior suspension, a sixty-day revocation, or a one-hundred-twenty-day suspension, and how do suspensions affect your six-month permit clock?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: A junior permit, license, or privilege draws a sixty-day suspension for a serious violation of three or more points or two other violations, a sixty-day revocation if that pattern recurs within six months after restoration, and a one-hundred-twenty-day suspension for a texting or cell-phone conviction, and a junior permit must be held at least six months—excluding any suspension or revocation time—before scheduling a road test.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: How long does new-driver probation last for newly licensed adults, and what penalties hit first-round violations, repeats, or phone convictions?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: Licensed adults eighteen or older serve six months of probation, where DWAI, speeding, reckless driving, tailgating, speed contests or any two violations trigger sixty days off plus a fresh six-month probation, a repeat round revokes at least six months with probation after restoration, and texting or cell-phone use costs one hundred twenty days.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: How does temporary suspension contrast with revocation, and how does a junior texting conviction compare with sixty-day sanctions?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: Suspension borrows the license back after a wait while revocation destroys it and forces reapplication, and junior violations stack sixty-day clocks whereas texting jumps straight to one hundred twenty days.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: How does the trigger structure of junior sanctions differ from adult new-driver probation before either reaches revocation?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: Junior sanctions fire per violation pattern while adult probation watches a six-month window, and both ladders end in revocation only after repeated failure.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: What happens if you ignore a New York traffic ticket, and how are non-criminal moving tickets versus criminal charges routed in New York City?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.memory_hook: Answer tickets promptly, TVB handles city
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: Ticketed drivers must answer promptly or face indefinite suspension and possible default conviction, and city tickets for non-criminal moving violations go through the Traffic Violations Bureau while criminal driving charges stay in the regular courts.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: Where are traffic tickets heard outside New York City, and what representation right does every motorist keep?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: Outside the city, traffic cases land in the city, county, town or village criminal and traffic court where the offense happened, and every ticketed motorist may mount a defense with a lawyer.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: Which outside jurisdictions actually post moving convictions and points onto a non-commercial New York driving record?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.memory_hook: Only Ontario and Quebec post points
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: Out-of-state moving convictions of non-commercial licensees go unrecorded except offenses in Ontario and Quebec, and only those two provinces feed the violation-point record.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: What happens if you ignore an out-of-state moving summons from most states, and which listed exception states stay outside that compact?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: Ignoring an out-of-state moving ticket suspends the New York license until answered and proven satisfied, except tickets from Alaska, California, Michigan, Montana, Oregon, Virginia and Wisconsin, a list the text calls six states, with mirror suspension at home for other states drivers who snub a New York summons.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: Why is paying an out-of-state speeding ticket smart even though most states never add points to your New York record?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: Out-of-state convictions vanish except Ontario and Quebec, yet ignoring any out-of-state ticket still suspends, so recording and answering are opposite rules.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: How long does New York revoke your license after an out-of-state or Canadian alcohol, drug, or fatal driving conviction?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.memory_hook: Outside DWI revokes ninety, youth year
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: Out-of-state or Canadian alcohol or drug driving convictions revoke New York licenses at least ninety days from age twenty-one up, at least one year or until twenty-one whichever runs longer below that age, and any-state criminal negligence, homicide or assault convictions from fatal driving revoke the license and possibly registrations too.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: Beyond highway vehicles, which recreational privileges face matching underage-drinking sanctions for operators under twenty-one?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: Suspension and revocation have many mandatory triggers, and motorboat and snowmobile operators under twenty-one who drink face matching sanctions on those privileges.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: What are the minimum license sanctions for Aggravated DWI, standard DWI, alcohol DWAI, drug DWAI, and out-of-state DUI?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.memory_hook: Aggravated year, DWI six, DWAI ninety
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: Aggravated DWI at point-one-eight blood alcohol revokes at least one year, plain DWI at point-zero-eight revokes at least six months, alcohol-impaired driving suspends ninety days, drug-impaired driving revokes at least six months, and out-of-state DUI revokes ninety days to six months by conviction.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: How long is your license revoked for refusing a chemical test as an adult, five-year repeat offender, or driver under twenty-one?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: Refusing a chemical test revokes at least one year past twenty-one, eighteen months with a refusal or alcohol or drug violation inside five years, at least one year for a first under-twenty-one refusal, until twenty-one or one year whichever is longer for a second, and at least one year for Zero Tolerance refusals.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: What factors scale chemical-test refusal revocations compared with alcohol and drug conviction sanctions?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: Refusals scale with age and history from one year to eighteen months to until-twenty-one, while violations scale with substance from ninety-day DWAI suspension up to year-long aggravated revocation.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: How harshly does New York revoke drivers under twenty-one convicted of alcohol or drug offenses, including youthful-offender findings?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: Under-twenty-one arrests ending in any listed alcohol or drug conviction revoke at least one year, a second while still under twenty-one runs one year or until twenty-one whichever is longer, and youthful-offender and out-of-state cases count the same.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: Which blood-alcohol band triggers New York's Zero Tolerance law under twenty-one, and what are the first and second sanctions?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: Zero Tolerance suspends under-twenty-one licenses six months for blood alcohol from point-zero-two to point-zero-seven, a level one drink can reach, and a second offense revokes one year or until twenty-one whichever is longer.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: How does the six-month Zero Tolerance suspension compare with the penalty for refusing a Zero Tolerance breath test?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: Zero Tolerance punishes the low band from point-zero-two to point-zero-seven with six months off, while refusing its test costs a full year, so refusal dwarfs the underlying sip.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: Which four speeding, school-bus, hit-and-run, or street-racing triggers bring a mandatory revocation of at least six months?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: Revocation of at least six months follows three speeding or misdemeanor traffic violations within eighteen months dated by offense, three stopped-school-bus passings within three years, one injury or fatal scene-leaving, or one speed contest, with a second contest inside twelve months stretching to at least one year.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: What happens if you drive, lend, or crash an uninsured vehicle, or cancel insurance on a parked car without returning plates?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: Driving or lending an uninsured vehicle, or crashing uninsured, revokes at least one year, lapsed coverage means surrendering plates and registration, and parked off-road vehicles still need their plates returned or civil and suspension penalties follow.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: Which four reporting or financial defaults trigger an indefinite New York license suspension until resolved?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: Skipping a crash report, child support, taxes or a crash court judgment suspends indefinitely until the underlying condition is fixed.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: Why does New York say preventable crash instead of accident, and can a fatal crash cost your license without a ticket?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: Preventable crashes replaced accidents in the vocabulary, and a fatal crash can suspend or revoke after a hearing even with no violation charged at the scene.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: What criminal penalties apply to driving while suspended or revoked, and what happens at ten or twenty unanswered-ticket suspensions?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: Suspended or revoked driving is criminal with two-hundred-to-five-thousand-dollar fines plus possible jail or probation and vehicle seizure, worse when intoxicated on an alcohol suspension, severe past ten ticket-ignoring suspensions, and criminal past twenty even without driving at arrest.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: How does hitting twenty ignored-ticket suspensions cross into criminal liability even when someone is not behind the wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: Driving suspended is criminal with fines, jail risk and seizure, and twenty ignored-ticket suspensions make it criminal even for a non-driver, so the count itself becomes the crime.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: Where does New York's point table apply besides public streets, when do single offenses act alone, and what accompanies sanctions?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: The point system hunts persistent violators through a violation table that also governs public parking lots, single violations alone rarely force action except alcohol, drug or aggravated unlicensed cases, and every vehicle and traffic violation adds fines on top of license sanctions.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: How many points attach to child-seat faults, employer brake faults, texting or injury hit-and-run, work-zone speeding, and refusals?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.memory_hook: Texting five, work-zone eight, refusal eleven
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: The table plainly pairs texting while driving, facilitating aggravated unlicensed operation, and leaving an injury scene at five points each, construction-zone speeding at eight, aggravated unlicensed operation and chemical-test refusals at eleven, child-restraint violations at three, and inadequate brakes on an employer vehicle at four.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: Which everyday moving violations appear on New York's point table, and how are speeding points structured?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: The same table also rates reckless driving, school-bus passing, railroad crossings, signal and sign disobedience, passing and lane faults, property-damage leaving, and most other moving violations, with speeding split into bands from one-to-ten through over forty miles over the limit.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: How many points in what timeframe trigger suspension, how are dates measured, and what is the sole defense at a point hearing?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: Points count from the offense date, eleven or more within twenty-four months brings a mailed suspension notice, and the only hearing argument is mistaken identity, never re-arguing guilt or pleading hardship.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: What point and insurance relief does an approved crash-prevention course grant, and what three things can it never do?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: An approved crash-prevention course cuts up to four points and ten percent of liability and collision premiums, yet never stops a mandatory sanction, banks no future credit, and trims no responsibility assessment.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: Why can a crash-prevention course lower your point total yet fail to stop a three-speeding revocation or shrink a state assessment?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: The crash course erases points and premiums but never halts a mandatory sanction, banks no future credit, and shrinks no assessment, so relief and rescue differ.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: What fee ends a standard fixed-term suspension, and what two charges end a Zero Tolerance suspension?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: Fixed-term suspensions end only after a fifty-dollar termination fee, while Zero Tolerance suspensions demand a one-hundred-twenty-five-dollar civil penalty plus a one-hundred-dollar termination fee.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: What is New York's standard reapplication fee after revocation, and which two situations waive that fee?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: Revocation usually requires a one-hundred-dollar reapplication fee, waived for no-insurance revocations and for conditional or restricted-use licenses.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: Who receives automated school-bus stop-arm camera fines, and what fine tiers apply across eighteen months as stated in the manual?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: A twenty-nineteen law lets school districts and towns use bus stop-arm cameras against owners who pass a stopped loading bus with reds flashing, fining two hundred fifty dollars first, twenty-seven second within eighteen months, and three hundred third and beyond within eighteen months, as extracted.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: What civil penalties must be paid before relicensing after an uninsured revocation or a first, commercial, or repeat chemical refusal?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: Before relicensing after revocation, uninsured operation or crashes cost a seven-hundred-fifty-dollar civil penalty, refusals five hundred or five hundred fifty in a commercial vehicle, and repeat-alcohol refusals within five years seven hundred fifty.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: How does the civil penalty on a one-year uninsured revocation compare with first and repeat chemical-refusal penalties?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: No-insurance revocations pair a year off with a seven-hundred-fifty-dollar penalty, while refusals pair revocation with five hundred, or seven hundred fifty on a five-year repeat.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: How much does New York's Driver Responsibility Assessment charge per year and across three years after an alcohol, drug, or refusal case?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: Aggravated DWI, DWI, any DWAI variant, or a chemical refusal each trigger a yearly two-hundred-fifty-dollar responsibility assessment for three years, on top of all other fines, with non-payment suspending every credential.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: At what point total inside eighteen months does New York's point assessment start, what does it cost yearly, and can PIRP reduce it?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.memory_hook: Six points: hundred yearly, twenty-five extra
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: Six points inside eighteen months trigger one hundred dollars yearly for three years plus twenty-five per extra point per year, the assessment reaches motorboat and snowmobile cases at times, and no crash-prevention course shrinks it.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: How do the three-year alcohol assessment and the three-year point assessment compare, and can one driver owe both?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: Alcohol convictions bill two hundred fifty yearly for three years regardless of points, while point totals bill one hundred plus twenty-five per extra point yearly, so the same driver can owe on both tracks.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: How does the six-point-in-eighteen-months threshold differ in consequence from the eleven-point-in-twenty-four-months threshold?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: Eleven points in twenty-four months suspends by mail with identity-only hearings, while six points in eighteen months bills money instead, two point clocks with two different teeth.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: What are New York's baseline rules on keeping right, passing side, dodging hazards, and your speed limit while overtaking?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Watch the speed-limit exam trap: accelerating above the posted limit just to finish a pass faster is illegal.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: How much lane width belongs to a motorcycle when you overtake it, even if the rider hugs one edge of a wide lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Riders shift across their lane constantly to dodge potholes, oil streaks, and wind blasts from passing trucks.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: Which side and clearance rule govern overtaking a bicyclist from behind in New York?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Cutting back right before your rear bumper clears the bicycle clips the rider's front wheel.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: How does the lane rule for passing a motorcycle differ from the clearance rule for passing a bicycle?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Motorcycles always command a complete separate lane, whereas bicycles command wide left clearance until safely past.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: How far ahead must you signal a lane change, and what rule applies when a car stops ahead at a crosswalk?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Passing a car halted at a crosswalk invites striking the hidden pedestrian that caused them to stop.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: Under which seven line, sight, oncoming-distance, curve, rail, or bridge conditions is passing on the left illegal on two-way roads?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Memorize both New York numbers: never pass with oncoming cars inside two hundred feet or within one hundred feet of rails or bridges.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: Which mirror, signal, and shoulder checks govern pulling left to pass and returning to the right lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Waiting until you see the overtaken car's entire front bumper in your rearview mirror prevents chopping across their hood.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: How does your blind-spot check before pulling out to pass differ from your visual check before returning right?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Side mirrors leave blind zones on both flanks, requiring a left head check going out and a mirror-plus-right check returning.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: Under which two conditions may you pass on the right on a two-way road, and what shoulder rule applies?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Dropping tires onto paved shoulders or across white edge stripes to squeeze past a left-turner is illegal unless directed.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: When may you pass on the right along a one-way street, and what hazards must you scan for at intersections?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Passing on the right through city intersections hides left-turning cross risks ahead and skaters or cyclists hugging the curb.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: How many bans restrict New York's default left pass compared with the conditions that unlock a right pass?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Treating left passes as standard and right passes as three narrow exceptions keeps lane discipline predictable for everyone.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: How should you adjust speed and lane position while being overtaken, and what does repeated right-side passing tell you?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Speeding up to trap a passing car in an oncoming lane creates head-on danger; ease off slightly instead.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: What do flashing yellow roof lights on the front and back of a New York school bus signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Accelerating to beat yellow bus flashers guarantees running illegal red lights seconds later when the door opens.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: Where and how far back must both directions halt when a stopped school bus flashes red lights in New York?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: New York's twenty-foot bus stop law applies inside school driveways and campus parking lots, not just public streets.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: When may stopped drivers move past a New York school bus, and does a divided highway median exempt oncoming lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Huge New York exam distinction: unlike many states, you must stop for red-flashing school buses even across divided highway medians.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: Why must you creep slowly and scan curbs even after a school bus turns off its red lights and rolls forward?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Most fatal school-bus tragedies strike children darting across pavement outside the bus rather than riders seated inside.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: How does New York treat stopped flashing buses equipped and marked to transport people with disabilities?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Wheelchair lifts take longer to load and unload, demanding the exact same twenty-foot stop patience.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: Contrast your obligation under flashing yellow roof lights against flashing red school-bus lights?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Yellow gives you space to brake smoothly so you come to rest at least twenty feet shy of red.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: How do court fines and license revocation scale from a first school-bus passing conviction to three convictions in three years?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Three convictions inside three years reach up to a thousand-dollar fine and strip your license for at least six months.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: How much does New York's stop-arm camera law bill vehicle owners for first, second, and third violations within eighteen months?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Automated stop-arm cameras mail escalating civil bills straight to the registered owner across an eighteen-month window.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: How does an officer's stop-bus conviction against the driver differ from an automated stop-arm camera ticket?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Roadside convictions hit the driver's record and license up to a thousand dollars, whereas camera citations bill the car's owner.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: Which seven core topics round out New York's passing chapter review?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Mastering mirror-bumper returns, crosswalk stop bans, and divided-highway bus stops locks down the highest-tested passing questions.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: Roughly how many traffic crashes happen in New York each year, and which two emergency items should every driver carry in the vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Even spotless defensive drivers can get caught in someone else's mistake among three hundred thousand yearly crashes.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: Must you stop after even a minor collision — and how does New York classify fleeing a property-only scene versus an injury or fatal scene?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Driving off from a bent bumper brings a traffic violation, while fleeing any hurt or killed victim escalates straight into a crime.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: What legal line separates leaving a property-damage crash from leaving a crash where someone was injured or killed?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: Permit questions test that crisp split between a traffic-law offense on sheet-metal damage and criminal prosecution when people get hurt.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: When a crash causes only property damage, which specific credentials and insurance details must you share with other drivers and police?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Do not stop at trading phone numbers — New York requires policy numbers, effective dates, registration, and showing your insurance card.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: What two options satisfy New York law if you damage a parked car, other property, or a domestic animal?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Striking a neighbor's dog, cat, mailbox, or parked sedan triggers the exact same duty to find the owner or notify officers.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: What two emergency confirmations must happen immediately whenever a crash injures or kills someone?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Never assume another bystander already dialed — verify both police and medical rescue units are actively on the way.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: How should you position drivable vehicles after a crash, and what fire hazard limits where you set flares?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Spilled gasoline vapors ignite instantly near striking flares, so check for leaking fuel and use reflective triangles when needed.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: If you were not involved in a crash and emergency help has already arrived, how should you drive past?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Rubbernecking slows emergency access and causes secondary rear-end collisions right beside responders.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: Under what sole threat may you move an injured crash victim, and how must you support their neck and spine if forced to drag them?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Cradling the neck between your upper arms while dragging lengthwise by clothing keeps a fractured spine straight away from flames.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: How does ordinary crash care contrast with fire-threatened crash care for an injured person?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Twisting an injured victim's neck in a non-burning car risks permanent paralysis when paramedics have backboards minutes away.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: What should bystanders outside and passengers trapped inside do when fallen electrical wires touch a crashed vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Stepping one foot from an energized car onto wet ground completes a lethal electrical circuit through your body.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: How does the downed-wire rule protect both approaching helpers and people sitting inside a wire-contacted car?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Rubber tires and cabin space shield occupants until utility and rescue crews safely de-energize the fallen line.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: Which injuries, fatalities, or single-person property-damage amounts require filing a written crash report with New York DMV?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Once damage to any one person's property tops one thousand dollars — or anyone is hurt — written DMV reporting becomes mandatory.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: Why does even a minor bruise trigger a DMV crash report while a small bumper scratch might not?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Personal harm has zero dollar minimum in New York, whereas property-only crashes trigger DMV forms above one thousand dollars.
sec12-card-sec12-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Every injury reports, damage past thousand

visual_sync.text_span: Every injury reports, damage past thousand

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: Within how many days must a required DMV crash report arrive, what penalty hits late filers, and who files if the driver is incapacitated?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Skipping the ten-day state form is a misdemeanor that can suspend or revoke both the driver's license and the owner's registration.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: Does reporting a crash to your auto insurance company satisfy New York's ten-day legal filing rule?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Many drivers lose their licenses assuming their insurance agent filed with Albany, when the legal ten-day duty stays on you.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: Which road users share New York streets with cars, where do child pedestrians cluster most, and how should you check driveways before backing?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Toddlers crouch below trunk-lid height in residential driveways, so walking behind your car before reversing prevents tragic back-over crashes.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: Which way must roadside pedestrians face, where do turning drivers scan for walkers, and who holds absolute crossing priority even over traffic signals?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Even when your light turns green, a blind pedestrian using a guide dog or white or metallic cane keeps full right-of-way.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: What share of city pedestrian injuries strike during left turns, and which habits or distractions must drivers eliminate?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Windshield A-pillars and oncoming-car gaps pull your eyes away from the far crosswalk right as you accelerate into a left turn.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: How do marked and unmarked intersection crosswalks compare when no traffic signal works, and where should your bumper stop for sightlines?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Every intersection corner carries legal crosswalk protection regardless of paint stripes, and hanging back preserves clear sightlines for adjacent lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: How must New York drivers behave around disabled walkers, flashing school buses, cars stopped at crosswalks, and blind windshield pillars?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Overtaking a car paused at an intersection or blocking a crosswalk traps hidden walkers directly in front of moving bumpers.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: What equal rule governs painted versus unpainted crosswalks, and which two stopped vehicles freeze all passing?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: New York permit questions pair unmarked corner crossings with the strict ban on passing stopped school buses or crosswalk yielders.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: Before turning, parking, or opening a car door — and while overtaking a bicyclist — what checks and passing adjustments keep riders safe?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Flinging a street-side door open without a shoulder check doors unsuspecting cyclists, and fast close passes buffet light frames sideways.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: Where do New York cyclists ride, how many may ride side-by-side, and which ages must wear approved bike helmets statewide?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: State law mandates approved helmets from age one through thirteen, while cities or counties can set broader local rules.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: Which two maneuvers let a cyclist leave the right curb or bike lane, and where does statewide youth helmet law cap?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Expect cyclists to merge inward well ahead of left turns or broken pavement rather than hugging gutters past hazards.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: How may a cyclist signal a right turn, which infants are banned as bike passengers, and how soon must serious bike crashes be reported?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Babies younger than twelve months can never ride on a bicycle, and serious-injury or fatal bike crashes trigger DMV filing within ten days.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: What audible device, brake rule, reflectors, and nighttime lamp distances must a road-ridden New York bicycle carry?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Notice New York requires a bell or horn audible one hundred feet away — whistles or sirens never qualify on bicycles.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: At what exact distances must a bicycle's front headlight, rear taillight, and side-visible light show after dark?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Memorizing that descending five-three-two hundred-foot staircase locks in one of New York's favorite equipment test numbers.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: How should you check right-rear blind zones on right-on-red turns, and may cars drive in green-painted bike lanes or bike boxes?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Sweeping right-rear mirrors and blind spots before turning right stops classic right-hook collisions across dedicated cycle tracks.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: How should motorists approach inline skaters, skateboarders, and scooter riders — and how do motorcycle legal rights compare with cars?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Small scooter and skate wheels catch easily on cracks at intersections, while motorcyclists carry full vehicle rights and duties.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: Why must drivers watch for motorcycles outside summer months, and why do riders suffer worse crash injuries despite helmets and eye gear?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Warm spring or autumn afternoons bring motorcycles out unexpectedly after drivers grow rusty looking for exposed two-wheelers.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: Why do motorcycles fool speed and distance judgment, and what lane-sharing rule applies to two motorcycles versus cars?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Vans and SUVs easily hide a narrow bike in adjacent lanes, and riders shift left or right inside their lane to see ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: Who may legally ride side-by-side inside a single New York traffic lane — and what sharing or passing move is banned?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Permit questions test both halves: two motorcyclists may pair up, yet neither bikes nor cars can share or split a mixed lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: Which four lighting or signal quirks can make a motorcycle blend into traffic or send a false turn cue?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Because motorcycles lack high center brake lights and many blinkers stay flashing until thumb-canceled, verify actual slowing before pulling out.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: What percentage of fatal two-vehicle motorcycle crashes involve a vehicle turning left, and how must drivers retrain their intersection scan?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Training your brain to actively search for helmets and single headlamps alongside trucks and buses breaks deadly left-turn tunnel vision.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: Why does the forty-one-percent fatal left-turn figure demand retraining car-seeking eyes at intersections?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: Oncoming straight-through motorcycles vanish right behind larger cars unless you pause and scan specifically for smaller silhouettes.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: How do gravel, railroad tracks, and steel bridge gratings affect motorcyclists ahead of you — and how should you follow?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Riders slow down, stand on pegs, and angle squarely across rail tracks or center up on open steel bridge decks.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: How does New York divide Class A, Class B, and Class C limited-use mopeds by top speed, required license, lane position, and gear?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Crossing thirty miles per hour into Class A triggers full motorcycle licensing, insurance, helmets, eye gear, and all-lane access.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: Which speed bands, license rules, and lane rights separate Class A mopeds from Class B and Class C?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Thirty miles per hour forms the clean dividing line where lower classes accept any license class inside right-hand lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: May mopeds enter expressways, who bears fault in most fatal car-truck crashes, and how far ahead does a long-hood truck's front blind spot stretch?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Four out of five people killed in car-truck wrecks sit inside the smaller passenger car, often after cutting inside that twenty-foot hood blind zone.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: Where do Class B, Class C, and Class A mopeds ride on surface streets versus expressways?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: High-speed limited-access highways stay off-limits to every moped class unless specific signage authorizes entry.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: Why do air-braked trucks take longer to stop, why shouldn't you linger alongside or tailgate them, and when may you merge back in front?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Air-brake pressure takes an extra moment to travel down long trailer lines before heavy drums even begin biting.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: Why does a long-hood tractor's twenty-foot front blind spot forbid tight lane cutoffs after passing?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Merging back before the entire tractor front fills your rearview mirror drops your trunk straight out of the trucker's sight.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: How should you pass a large truck, handle a backing rig, judge oncoming truck speed, and stop behind a truck on an upgrade?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Heavy manual rigs can roll backward several feet as the driver engages the clutch on a hill, so stop well back and slightly left.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: What does an orange rear triangle mark, how do ATVs or snowmobiles cross highways, and what horn rule applies near horses?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: Sounding a car horn near ridden or drawn horses is illegal in New York because a startled animal can bolt into traffic.
sec11-card-sec11-F21.must_match_memory_hook: Orange triangle slow, never honk horses

visual_sync.text_span: Orange triangle slow, never honk horses

sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: Which core sharing-the-road topics — from truck air brakes and bike three-abreast bans to blind walkers and horses — anchor New York's chapter review?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: Notice the review highlights that riding three bicycles abreast is illegal while two abreast stays lawful.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: Who may legally drive in New York, what minimum age applies to everyone, and what must new residents do within thirty days?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Even teens holding valid fifteen-year-old permits from other states cannot drive anywhere inside New York.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: What legal and licensing consequences follow forging or altering a motor-vehicle document?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Tampering with birth dates or expiration numbers turns an administrative issue into criminal prosecution.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: Which five weight, towing, passenger, bus, or cargo categories require a New York commercial license?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Notice New York counts fifteen passengers besides the driver when drawing its commercial passenger line.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: At what ages does a Class D license start, and what vehicle weights, trailer combinations, and mopeds does it cover?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Graduating an approved driver-education course unlocks full senior Class D privileges a full year early.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: How do size triggers and service triggers divide commercial vehicles from standard non-commercial vehicles?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Even light vans cross into commercial rules when carrying bus passengers or placarded hazmat.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: How do Class DJ and Class E compare with Class D in minimum age, weight limits, and for-hire passenger capacity?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Driving a taxi or livery sedan for fare up to fourteen riders demands Class E.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: How do age and driving purpose separate New York's Class D, Class DJ, and Class E operator licenses?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Remembering DJ for sixteen-year-old juniors and E for paid passenger carriage keeps operator classes clear.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: What ages apply to Class M and Class MJ motorcycle licenses, and how does New York print dual car-and-motorcycle privileges?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Adding motorcycle privileges merges both letters onto one single card rather than issuing two licenses.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: Which border crossings and flights accept a New York Enhanced license, who qualifies for one, and which license classes offer it?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Enhanced cards substitute for passports by land or sea yet never cover international flights.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: Where did the REAL ID standard originate, what can domestic flyers present at checkpoints, and where must you apply?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Because clerks inspect original proofs and snap fresh photos, initial REAL ID upgrades require office visits.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: Why can you cross into Canada by car with an Enhanced license yet not with a standard REAL ID?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Only the Enhanced card embeds citizenship proof for land and sea borders, whereas both board domestic planes.

sec01-card-sec01-F39.question_text: What proofs are required in-office for a REAL ID, and what card marking and MV-six hundred nineteen vision rules apply if you renew a standard card remotely?
sec01-card-sec01-F39.teaching_text: Skipping federal upgrades preserves online renewal convenience, though your plastic card prints a non-federal notice.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: When do Class D or E drivers need an R endorsement for personal RVs or rental trucks, and what tests and steps earn it?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Renting an oversized motorhome or household box truck without this road-test endorsement violates Class D limits.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: Which two measurements trigger the R endorsement, and how does its testing path differ from a regular license?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Even an underweight motorhome past forty feet long requires passing the R maneuver drive.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: Which form starts a first-time New York license, what steps follow, and how are first-license expiration and fees set?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Your initial card aligns to your birthday within five years, so age shapes exact fees.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: How many name-proof points must an applicant reach, what signature rule applies, and when is a New York photo card worth all six?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Once a New York photo card stays expired past two years, its standalone six-point shortcut vanishes.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: How do form MV-forty-four, the six-point signed-document tally, and a current New York photo card fit together at check-in?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Filling out your application form never substitutes for hitting six verified points with a signature.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: Which parent or agency statements, passports, consular IDs, and out-of-state or foreign photo licenses carry four identity points?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Notice parent statement MV-forty-five and valid passports carry four points, still needing two more.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: Which immigration, citizenship, military, benefit, and border-crossing photo documents count for three identity points?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Pairing two three-point military, permanent-resident, or benefit photo cards hits the six-point mark cleanly.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: Which school ID pairs, vehicle papers, military dependent cards, and Social Security cards earn two identity points?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Bringing a student photo badge without its matching report card or transcript forfeits those two points.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: Which vital-status records, permits, tribal or benefit cards, and recently expired immigration cards also earn two points?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Resident or work-authorization cards expired up to two years drop from three points down to two.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: Which banking, employment, insurance, utility, school-diploma, and tax items count for one identity point each?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Signed credit or debit cards often supply both the final point and the mandatory signature.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: Which remaining cards or tax records earn one point, and which six official documents separately prove date of birth?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: Observe that a birth certificate proves your age while adding zero points toward your name tally.
sec01-card-sec01-F17.must_match_memory_hook: Birth certificate or passport proves age

visual_sync.text_span: Birth certificate or passport proves age

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: What visual acuity must an applicant reach in at least one eye, and where are failures or special-lens cases routed?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: Passing with glasses or contacts adds a corrective-lens restriction whenever unaided sight falls short.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: Which four subjects appear on the twenty-question written test, and what overall and road-sign minimums are required to pass?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: Impaired-driving questions sit right alongside road signs and safe-driving habits on every twenty-question set.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: Why would scoring seventeen out of twenty still fail the New York permit test if you missed three sign questions?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Hitting seventy percent overall never rescues a test that gets fewer than two road signs right.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: Which extra manuals cover motorcycles and CDLs, and at what age can students take the high-school OKTA online knowledge pre-test?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: High-schoolers can knock out the knowledge test one month before turning sixteen at participating schools.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: How do the twenty-forty eye check, the written exam, and the high-school OKTA pre-test line up as separate steps?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Passing OKTA at school clears only the written hurdle while counter vision screening still awaits.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: Once a student passes or fails the school online test, what happens next for office application or retakes?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: Even after passing at fifteen years eleven months, permit issuance waits until your sixteenth birthday.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: How do New York junior driving rules define properly licensed, guardian, in loco parentis, and a qualifying school course?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Extracurricular sports or non-credit clubs never qualify as school courses under junior night rules.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.question_text: What daytime hours, supervisor rules, dual-brake requirements, and nighttime rules govern junior permits in New York City and Long Island?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.teaching_text: Practicing in the five boroughs without dual passenger-side brakes violates strict New York City permit law.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.question_text: Who may supervise an upstate junior permit holder from five morning to nine evening versus after nine evening?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.teaching_text: After nine evening upstate, a casual twenty-two-year-old friend can no longer legally supervise practice.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: How do New York's three regions compare on nighttime and daytime junior-permit practice?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Crossing county lines from Westchester into the Bronx after nine instantly makes junior-permit driving illegal.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.question_text: How are work, work-study, medical, and daycare trips defined, and which specific bridges, parks, test zones, and Westchester parkways ban learner permits?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.teaching_text: Even with a driving instructor beside you, entering road-test zones or listed Westchester parkways draws tickets.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: What baseline rule applies to every learner-permit supervisor statewide, and how do downstate rules tighten it?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: An older cousin licensed for cars qualifies upstate by day yet fails downstate supervisor rules.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.question_text: What passenger cap, belt and child-seat duty, and front-seat rule apply whenever a junior-permit holder drives?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.teaching_text: Nobody except your supervising driver may occupy the front passenger seat during learner practice.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.question_text: How many total, after-sunset, and heavy-traffic practice hours should candidates build, and what course is required before scheduling a road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.teaching_text: You cannot even book a New York road-test slot until your safe-driving course certificate clears.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.question_text: How long does a five-hour pre-licensing certificate stay valid, and does the defensive point-and-insurance course substitute for it?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.teaching_text: Taking an online insurance-discount class by mistake leaves you unable to schedule your road exam.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.question_text: How many points and what percentage of insurance rates can New York's crash-prevention course trim, and how often can it repeat?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.teaching_text: Completing an approved defensive class trims base liability and collision premiums across thirty-six months.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.question_text: What benefits does the Point and Insurance Reduction Program deliver, and why do permit holders still need a separate pre-licensing course?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.teaching_text: DMV exams love testing that discount defensive courses never unlock road-test booking for permit holders.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.question_text: What are the exact point, month, percentage, and year numbers for PIRP, and how does it relate to the Safe Driving Course?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.teaching_text: Keep the eighteen-month point window distinct from the three-year insurance discount and pre-licensing rules.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.question_text: How long must a junior permit stay valid before testing, what three papers come to the road test, and how do seventeen-year-olds upgrade?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.teaching_text: Forgetting signed parent certification form MV-two hundred sixty-two turns junior candidates away curb-side.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: How do the fifty-hour practice breakdown and the six-month valid-permit rule compare before a junior road test?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: Both the six-month valid hold and certified practice hours guard teens from rushing into road tests.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.question_text: What must every test vehicle and accompanying driver meet at arrival, and what extra vehicle must a motorcycle candidate provide?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.teaching_text: Motorcycle examiners ride inside a separate chase vehicle driven by your licensed escort during testing.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.question_text: What separate purpose does each road-test form serve across MV-two hundred seventy-eight, MV-two hundred eighty-five, and MV-two hundred sixty-two?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.teaching_text: Keeping those three form numbers straight prevents scrambling at the curb before your examiner approaches.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.question_text: How do you drive legally right after passing your New York road test while waiting about two weeks for the mailed card?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.teaching_text: Your downloadable interim license needs your original photo learner permit carried alongside it until mail arrives.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.question_text: What non-family young-passenger cap, seat-belt duty, and regional restrictions still bind teens after passing the road test onto Class DJ?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.teaching_text: Earning a junior license lifts learner supervision on allowed routes yet keeps peer-passenger caps strict.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.question_text: Which exact employment or enrollment documents must a junior licensee carry for solo job, farm, or school travel on Long Island and upstate?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.teaching_text: Driving solo past curfew to work or night classes without signed schedule paperwork counts as violating restrictions.

sec01-card-sec01-R15.question_text: How does a junior driver's solo destination determine whether to carry form MV-58A, an employer letter, or school letterhead?
sec01-card-sec01-R15.teaching_text: Showing a work form while driving home from an evening college lab fails roadside checks.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.question_text: Where and when may a Class DJ junior license holder drive solo during daytime and nighttime across NYC, Long Island, and upstate?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.teaching_text: Notice New York City bans junior nighttime driving completely even after you hold a junior license.
