visual_sync.text_span: Free days outside NYC, restricted nights

sec01-card-sec01-R14.question_text: How do after-nine-evening rules for a Class DJ license split across New York City, Long Island, and upstate?
sec01-card-sec01-R14.teaching_text: Long Island night solos allow school and farm runs yet surprisingly exclude ordinary retail jobs.
sec01-card-sec01-R14.must_match_memory_hook: City zero, Island school-farm, upstate work-school

visual_sync.text_span: City zero, Island school-farm, upstate work-school

sec01-card-sec01-F37.question_text: What passenger and quarter-mile supervision rules govern learner-permit and junior motorcycle or moped riders?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.teaching_text: Even on a single-seat bike or moped, your licensed motorcycle supervisor trails within one-quarter mile.

sec01-card-sec01-R16.question_text: Who is the only permissible passenger on a Class M or MJ permit or junior license, and how close must supervision stay?
sec01-card-sec01-R16.teaching_text: Losing sight past a quarter mile breaks legal supervision for both permit and junior motorcyclists.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.question_text: How fast must you report a New York address change, what do you write on your card, and how early can you renew?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.teaching_text: Unlike thirty-day newcomer swaps, moving within New York gives just ten days to notify DMV.
sec01-card-sec01-F38.must_match_memory_hook: Report moves ten days, ink back

visual_sync.text_span: Report moves ten days, ink back

sec01-card-sec01-F40.question_text: How can active-duty service members extend a New York license, and what deadline binds newly settled residents?
sec01-card-sec01-F40.teaching_text: Filing form MV-seventy-five within sixty days of entering active service preserves expiration protection past discharge.
sec01-card-sec01-F40.must_match_memory_hook: Duty plus six months, thirty-day resident

visual_sync.text_span: Duty plus six months, thirty-day resident

sec01-card-sec01-F41.question_text: How do transfer steps differ between US or Canadian newcomers and other-country newcomers, including keeping a foreign card from destruction?
sec01-card-sec01-F41.teaching_text: Without filing a written hold request, surrendered non-Canadian foreign licenses get destroyed after issuance.

sec01-card-sec01-R17.question_text: How does New York summarize newcomer testing by origin alongside the rules for young out-of-state visitors?
sec01-card-sec01-R17.teaching_text: Visiting seventeen-year-olds must obey both their home-state restrictions and New York's regional junior curfews.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: Who must yield when you approach an intersection on a fresh green light while another driver is still mid-intersection turning left?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: A fresh green light never grants license to ram a driver still clearing a turn started on the previous phase.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: When opposite-direction drivers arrive together, who holds priority, and how should a left-turning driver stage and keep their wheels while waiting?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Turning your front wheels left while waiting mid-intersection shoves your car straight into oncoming traffic if rear-ended.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: At an uncontrolled crossroads or when two right-angle vehicles stop at the exact same moment, which driver yields?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Even when both drivers plan to travel straight through, the vehicle sitting to the left yields priority.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: How do opposite-arrival left turns and simultaneous right-angle stops both place the yielding duty on leftness?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Pairing opposite left-turn yields with cross-street left-driver yields locks both New York intersection tiebreakers into one habit.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: What stop, yield, and directional-looking rules apply when pulling out of a New York driveway, parking lot, or private road?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Drivers turning right out of a busy lot stare left at cars and miss sidewalk runners approaching from the right.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: How does your legal duty exiting a private driveway contrast with entering an intersection on a green signal?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Private exits enter public flow from zero priority, whereas green-light traffic yields only to users still clearing inside.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: How must New York drivers treat pedestrians and cyclists at painted or unmarked crosswalks, including stragglers after the light turns green?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Turning left or right on green still requires checking the destination crosswalk before swinging across walkers or bikes.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: When must you hold back behind the line even though your traffic signal shows steady green?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Gridlocking an intersection or offset side street traps emergency responders and earns steep urban box-blocking tickets.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: Who holds the right-of-way when your vehicle approaches a New York traffic circle or rotary?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Forcing your nose ahead of cars already curving around the central island disrupts continuous rotary flow.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: How must every direction respond to approaching fire, ambulance, or police vehicles flashing red combinations, even without a siren?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: New York police cars do not have to run sirens alongside flashing red or red-blue lights to command your stop.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: Which ordinary traffic rules may authorized emergency drivers break when running lights and sirens, and why must you stay alert?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: An ambulance or fire engine can legally push past red lights or reverse down a one-way block during emergencies.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: What speed and lane actions does New York's Move Over law require past stopped emergency, hazard, or shoulder-parked highway vehicles?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: On New York parkways and controlled-access interstates, Move Over protects any disabled car parked on the shoulder, not just police.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: Which volunteer or service drivers use solo blue, green, or amber lights in New York, and are they authorized emergency vehicles?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Exam questions test that volunteer blue firefighter and green medic lamps ask for courtesy yielding while obeying all laws.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: Compare your legal obligations across red-flashing emergency rigs, solo blue-green-amber courtesy lights, and shoulder-stopped highway vehicles?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Mixing up mandatory red-light pullovers with courtesy blue or green lamps is a classic New York written-test trap.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: At least how many feet ahead must you signal every turn or lane change in New York, and should you signal before braking?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Flicking your blinker before touching the brake pedal tells drivers behind you why your brake lights are about to glow.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: Why must turn prep double-check for motorcycles, keep front wheels straight, mind rear-wheel tracking, and scan low beside right curbs?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Failure to spot an approaching motorcycle causes most car-motorcycle crashes, while rear tires track tighter toward right-corner strollers.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: How close to the right edge should you approach and finish a standard right turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Swinging wide left before turning right fools trailing drivers and cyclists into squeezing up your right flank.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: Which lane do you start from and land in when turning left from a one-way street onto another multi-lane one-way street?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Starting and landing tight along both left edges keeps the tighter inside corner clear without crossing outer lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: How do you position your car when turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Muscle memory from leaving a one-way left curb must not trick you into entering the oncoming left half of a two-way street.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: Where do you stage, pass inside the intersection, and land when turning left from one two-way street onto another?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: Turning slightly left of the intersection's midpoint lets two opposing left-turners pass nose-to-nose without tangling paths.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: Where do you stage, turn relative to the intersection center, and land when turning left from a two-way road onto a one-way road?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Because no oncoming traffic uses the cross street's far left lane, you turn before the center point directly into it.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: Which lane must you enter first when turning left from a two-way road onto a four-lane highway, and how do you move right afterward?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Sweeping straight across into the outer right lane mid-turn cuts off opposing right-turners who legally own that curb lane.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: What single staging rule unites all five New York left turns, and how do two-way versus one-way landings split?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Start as far left on your legal side as allowed, then hug the centerline on two-ways or the left curb on one-ways.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: What safer turnaround beats a highway U-turn, and which lane position and arrow rule govern legal U-turns?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Swinging a U-turn from an outer right lane crosses blind parallel traffic from behind.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: List the five places or sight-distance limits where U-turns are illegal in New York, and what maneuver replaces them on narrow streets?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Paved police crossovers through expressway medians remain strictly off-limits to everyday motorists.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: Contrast the lane and five-hundred-foot visibility rules for legal U-turns against the four zones that ban them outright?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Even clear dry sight past five hundred feet cannot legalize a U-turn inside a school zone or Manhattan business block.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: Walk through the signals, traffic scans, steering locks, and curb stops of a New York road-test three-point turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Bumping either curb with your tires or forgetting either turn signal loses easy points on the New York road test.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: Put the four ordered steps of a New York three-point turn in exact sequence from right-edge stop to driving away?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Scanning both directions before every leg—forward across, backing right, and pulling away—keeps narrow two-way turnarounds crash-free.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: Which hands-on parking maneuver appears on every New York road test, and what sign and parking rules pair with it?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Examiners score your parallel park on every drive while the written exam drills the three no-series curb signs.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: If your car has backup cameras, parking sensors, or auto-park features, who bears legal responsibility and what must you still do?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Relying purely on dashboard screens without turning your head to check behind fails road tests and misses darting kids.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: How far beside the lead car do you stop, what checks come next, and where do you look as you angle back?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Stopping roughly two feet alongside the front car sets the right pivot geometry before locking wheels toward the curb.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: When do you turn the wheel the opposite way while backing in, and what is your maximum legal distance from the curb?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Finishing more than twelve inches out from the curb leaves your left side jutting into traffic and costs road-test points.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: How do you inch closer if parked too far from the curb, and what rule governs opening street-side doors?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Swinging a street-side door into a cyclist or passing fender puts legal fault squarely on the parked occupant.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: What three brake, gear, and front-wheel steps secure a vehicle parked on a hill in New York?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Angling tires so the curb catches any roll stops a slipped brake from sending two tons downhill into traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: How do you position your wheels and vehicle inside a tight parallel space before merging out into traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Backing straight toward the rear car creates the front-end clearance needed to clear the lead bumper cleanly.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: Walk through the exact six-step window, mirror, signal, and shoulder-check sequence for pulling out of a parallel space?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Starting over your right shoulder checks sidewalk walkers and rear clearance before your signal and left-shoulder traffic checks.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: Which shoulder check opens and which shoulder checks close the six-step scan out of a right-curb parallel space?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Road-test examiners watch your chin to verify you checked behind through the rear window before glancing left into traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: How does New York define parking, standing, and stopping?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Knowing whether cargo loading counts separates legal curbside errands from instant urban tickets.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: What activity is still legal at a No Parking sign, a No Standing sign, and a No Stopping sign?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: At a No Standing sign you can drop off or pick up passengers quickly, provided the driver stays behind the wheel.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: How do No Parking, No Standing, and No Stopping signs tighten curbside restrictions step by step?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Exam questions test what disappears at each rung: first unattended cars, next packages and driver exits, finally all voluntary stops.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: Where is stopping, standing, or parking completely banned, and what single exception applies within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: New York lets you pause within fifteen feet of a hydrant only if a licensed driver sits ready to move immediately.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: What distance bans govern parking or standing near driveways, crosswalks, signs or signals, firehouses, cut curbs, and railroad crossings?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Notice the opposite-curb firehouse twist: twenty feet on the station side jumps to seventy-five feet across the street.
sec07-card-sec07-F12.must_match_memory_hook: Twenty crosswalk, thirty sign, fifty rail

visual_sync.text_span: Twenty crosswalk, thirty sign, fifty rail

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: Match fifteen, twenty, thirty, and fifty feet to the four curb hazards they protect in New York?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Drilling those four ascending numbers in order locks down one of the most frequent distance questions on the permit quiz.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: What credentials and passenger requirement must be met to use a disability parking space on streets or in shopping centers?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Borrowing a relative's hanging placard to park close while running solo errands violates New York law even with valid tags.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: What criminal or civil penalties hit applicants and certifying doctors who make false statements for disability plates versus permits?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: False plate applications trigger misdemeanor charges and mandatory license revocation, while permit fraud hits both applicant and doctor financially.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: Which DMV form requests disability plates or permits, and what rule governs diagonal-striped access aisles?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Straddling diagonal blue or white stripes beside a reserved stall traps wheelchair ramps and draws full disability-parking fines.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: Who sets street disability-parking fines, and what default fines plus surcharge apply in shopping-center lots?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Repeat shopping-lot violations inside two years in the same municipality double the base bracket up to one hundred fifty dollars.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: Contrast the license and criminal fallout of lying for disability plates against lying for a hanging permit?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Because plates attach to vehicle registration under state motor-vehicle law, plate fraud carries criminal revocation rather than civil fines alone.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: Which six core skills and curb rules appear in New York's parallel-parking review questions?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Reviewing twelve-inch curb spacing, street-side door checks, and passenger drop-offs under No Standing covers every road-test and quiz staple.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: What eight everyday habits form the foundation of defensive driving in New York?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Stacking good speed, space, signaling, seat belts, sobriety, vehicle upkeep, and pocketed phones stops emergencies before they form.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: How should you sit and grip the wheel, how far ahead should you scan, and what should you assume at side-road stop or yield signs?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Never bet your life that cross-street traffic will honor a stop plaque; stay poised to react.
sec08-card-sec08-F02.must_match_memory_hook: Both hands, scan far, expect runners

visual_sync.text_span: Both hands, scan far, expect runners

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: How do mental, visual, and manual distractions compare in danger, and how should phones, kids, and pets be handled inside the car?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Daydreaming or arguing steals reaction speed just as dangerously as taking eyes off traffic or hands off steering.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: Which unsafe road behaviors count as aggressive driving, and what exact line turns aggression into road rage?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Tailgating, shoulder passing, and running school buses break traffic laws, while trying to harm someone crosses into crime.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: If an aggressive driver confronts or follows you, how should you react with your eyes, lane, seat belts, and destination?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Pulling into your own driveway leads an angry follower home; head straight toward a police station or busy public help.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: What trip-planning, cabin, and mindset habits keep you from slipping into aggressive driving yourself?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Calling ahead when running late and giving up contested right-of-way trades five lost seconds for zero bent fenders.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: How does New York define road rage legally compared with aggressive driving, and what penalties can follow?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Violent intimidation behind the wheel triggers criminal prosecution carrying fines, probation, jail time, and license loss.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: What single shift turns an aggressive traffic violation like tailgating or chasing into criminal road rage?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Once anger aims to intimidate, assault, or injure another motorist, traffic court gives way to criminal charges.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: Which specific acts — from horn blasts and cutoffs to leaving the car — count as road rage, and how does rage wreck judgment and life?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Stepping out at a red light to confront someone or ramming bumpers can cost your freedom, career, and license.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: What are New York's default unposted speed limits statewide versus inside New York City, and can driving under the limit still draw a ticket?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Cruising at fifty on an icy fifty-five expressway still violates New York's reasonable-and-prudent speed law.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: Contrast the unposted speed cap across New York State with New York City, and explain why posted signs are fair-weather maximums?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Without a higher sign posted, city streets cap speed thirty miles per hour lower than open state roads.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: How large a share of rear-end wrecks come from tailgating, how do you time the two-second rule, and how do you shed tailgaters safely?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Tapping your brakes to scare off a tailgater invites the exact forty-percent rear-end crash pattern you want to avoid.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: When does New York's normal two-second following cushion stretch to at least three or four seconds?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Tall box trucks block your forward sightline and slick pavement doubles braking distance, demanding extra seconds.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: What does primary seat-belt enforcement mean in New York, and does the law cover out-of-state visitors as well as residents?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Officers need zero other traffic violation to pull a car over the moment they spot an unbuckled occupant.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: What fines and driver-license points apply for an unbuckled driver, an unbuckled rider sixteen or older, and an unrestrained child under sixteen?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Every unbuckled passenger under sixteen lands both a fine up to one hundred dollars and three points on the driver.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: How must children under four — including toddlers under two — and children ages four through seven be restrained in New York?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Adult seat belts ride across a young child's neck and belly without a booster positioning the lap-shoulder strap.
sec08-card-sec08-F13.must_match_memory_hook: Rear-facing to two, boosters to eight

visual_sync.text_span: Rear-facing to two, boosters to eight

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: What height or weight threshold guides moving children ages eight to fifteen — or oversized four-plus kids — onto vehicle belts, and which vehicles are exempt?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Body size governs real crash protection, keeping petite older kids in boosters until four-foot-nine or one hundred pounds.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: Match New York's three age brackets — under four, four to seven, and eight to fifteen — with seats, boosters, belts, and size swaps?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Rear-facing protects infants through age two, boosters bridge ages four to seven, and proper fit unlocks adult belts.
sec08-card-sec08-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Seat under four, booster under eight

visual_sync.text_span: Seat under four, booster under eight

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: How many inches should sit between your chest and the airbag cover, where do hands grip, and what infant rule is non-negotiable?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: An inflating front passenger airbag strikes the back of a rear-facing infant carrier with lethal force.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: Do New York work-zone speeding fines double when no workers are visible, and how should you merge, space, and pass mobile crews?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Rear-end crashes top work-zone collisions, so merge as soon as signs appear and hold at least two-plus seconds.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: Which way does roundabout traffic circle, what controls entries, and what speed limit caps vehicles inside the circle?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Curved entry deflection naturally slows cars down so circulating traffic flows smoothly at thirty miles per hour or below.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: As you roll up to a roundabout, which direction do you scan for gap priority, where do you stop for queues, and how do you treat bikes?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Keep crosswalks unblocked while waiting for a left-side gap, and never squeeze past a bicyclist riding inside the ring.
sec08-card-sec08-F18.must_match_memory_hook: Look left, yield, share with bikes

visual_sync.text_span: Look left, yield, share with bikes

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: Who holds right-of-way at a roundabout entrance, and which direction must approaching drivers look?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Because traffic circles counterclockwise around the island, vehicles already in the ring approach from your left with priority.
sec08-card-sec08-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Yield entry, scan left for gaps

visual_sync.text_span: Yield entry, scan left for gaps

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: Once inside a roundabout, how do drivers signal exits, where must pedestrians cross, and what two choices do bicyclists have?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Pedestrians never cut across the center island, using perimeter crosswalks and splitter islands one direction at a time.
sec08-card-sec08-F19.must_match_memory_hook: Signal right exiting, walkers use refuges

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: Pair a circling driver's right-of-way and exit signal with how pedestrians and cyclists navigate a roundabout?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Even though you hold priority inside the circle, stay ready to yield for walkers in the exit crosswalk.
sec08-card-sec08-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Inside holds priority, blink right exiting

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: How does fatigue hurt driving skills, which warning signs betray sleepiness, and which groups face the highest drowsy-crash risk?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Forgetting the last few miles or hitting shoulder rumble strips means microsleeps are already stealing control.
sec08-card-sec08-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Fatigue impairs like alcohol, watch drift

visual_sync.text_span: Fatigue impairs like alcohol, watch drift

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: How often should road-trippers stop for breaks, why fail cold air or loud radios, and how long do safe naps and caffeine take?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Rolling windows down only masks exhaustion briefly; pull into a safe rest area for a fifteen-to-forty-five-minute nap.
sec08-card-sec08-F21.must_match_memory_hook: Break every two hours, nap safely

visual_sync.text_span: Break every two hours, nap safely

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: What fines, license points, and junior-license suspensions hit drivers caught on handheld calls or texting within eighteen months?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Junior and probationary drivers lose privileges for one hundred twenty days on offense one and at least a year on quick repeats.
sec08-card-sec08-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Five call points, escalating text fines

visual_sync.text_span: Five call points, escalating text fines

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: How does a first handheld phone call ticket compare with texting tickets and junior-license penalties?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Repeat texting fines climb steeply inside eighteen months, and young drivers face suspension on either handheld offense.
sec08-card-sec08-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Calls add points, teen cards suspend

visual_sync.text_span: Calls add points, teen cards suspend

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: Besides New York's yearly inspection requirement, who bears ultimate legal responsibility for a vehicle's safe condition on the road?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Borrowing a friend's car with bald tires or dead brake lights still puts legal responsibility on the person driving.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: How do you dry wet brakes after a puddle, and what warning signs in brakes, power steering, or headlights demand prompt service?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Pressing the brake pedal lightly dries soaked linings, whereas pulling, spongy fade, or steering play demands immediate repair.
sec08-card-sec08-F24.must_match_memory_hook: Dry wet brakes, check steering, lights

visual_sync.text_span: Dry wet brakes, check steering, lights

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: What minimum tread depth and penny test check New York tires, what flaws ground a tire immediately, and how should horns be used?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Seeing the top of Lincoln's head upside down means tread is worn out, and horns warn of danger rather than anger.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: Which core defensive topics — from scanning and unposted city speed to belts, fatigue, rage, work zones, and roundabouts — anchor chapter review?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Locking these nine review checkpoints together prepares you for New York's highest-frequency defensive driving questions.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: What share of New York motor-vehicle deaths involve impaired driving, and how overrepresented are drivers under twenty-one in impaired fatal crashes?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Young drivers under twenty-one represent just four percent of licensed motorists yet seven percent of impaired fatal-crash operators.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: When does alcohol start impairing driving judgment, vision, and reaction speed, and why is night driving especially dangerous after drinking?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Alcohol slows pupil recovery from oncoming headlight glare and creates false confidence long before you look visibly drunk.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: Which illegal, cannabis, and prescription drugs make driving a crime when impaired, and what happens when substances combine with alcohol?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Combining alcohol with cannabis, street drugs, or even drowsiness-inducing prescriptions amplifies impairment and can turn fatal.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: Name New York's six alcohol and drug driving offenses, and match the blood alcohol thresholds over point-zero-five, point-zero-eight, and point-one-eight?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Saliva, urine, breath, or blood tests establish the reading that separates DWAI, standard DWI, and Aggravated DWI.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: How do New York's impairment, intoxication, and aggravated intoxication offenses step up from one rung to the next?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Drugs can trigger impairment or inability charges, while alcohol climbs cleanly from impairment through point-zero-eight to point-one-eight.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: Pair each of New York's three key adult decimal blood-alcohol readings cleanly with the offense it evidences?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Every upward jump in those decimals upgrades both the charge name on the ticket and the mandatory penalty floor.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: Can officer observations convict you without a chemical test, and what happens to your physical license at sentencing?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Even when a judge grants a twenty-day stay to wrap up affairs, the court confiscates your plastic card immediately.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: What does New York's Implied Consent law mean when arrested, and what three consequences hit a driver who refuses chemical testing?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Your license suspends at arraignment, prosecutors can tell the jury you refused, and DMV revokes after a hearing.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: If you beat the DWI charge in criminal court after refusing a breath or blood test, what still happens at DMV?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Administrative chemical-test refusal runs on an independent DMV track, so winning in court never restores a refused license.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: Which factors control blood alcohol, which four standard servings hold equal alcohol, and how fast does one drink clear?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: A shot, five-ounce wine glass, twelve-ounce beer, and twelve-ounce cooler pack identical pure alcohol, raising a man about point-zero-two.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: Why is switching from liquor to beer or wine never safer, and what three factors actually set blood alcohol content?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Fitness, willpower, and beverage style never shield your bloodstream when standard servings carry identical alcohol.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: How does eating food affect alcohol compared with coffee, exercise, or cold showers — and what alone lowers BAC?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Black coffee and cold water merely produce a wide-awake drunk driver while your liver processes alcohol on a fixed clock.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: Contrast what food, coffee, exercise, and cold showers actually do against the sole method that lowers blood alcohol?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Mistaking caffeine alertness for sobriety puts impaired drivers behind the wheel before time clears their bloodstream.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: What BAC range triggers New York's Zero Tolerance law for drivers under twenty-one, and what suspensions and fees hit first and repeat violations?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: First-timers face a six-month suspension plus two hundred twenty-five dollars in combined fees, while repeats revoke at least a year.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: How much lower is New York's Zero Tolerance trigger for drivers under twenty-one compared with adult alcohol impairment?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Because a single drink lifts blood alcohol around point-zero-two, even one beverage puts an underage driver in violation.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: What happens if you use a license or ID to illegally buy alcohol, or consume alcohol or cannabis in a vehicle on a public road?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Open alcohol containers or in-car cannabis use bring fines up to one hundred fifty dollars plus up to fifteen jail days.
sec09-card-sec09-F12.must_match_memory_hook: Fake purchases suspend, open containers jail

visual_sync.text_span: Fake purchases suspend, open containers jail

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: At point-one-eight or higher, what fines, jail ceilings, and revocations apply on a first Aggravated DWI versus a second inside ten years?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Repeating Aggravated DWI within ten years jumps to a felony carrying up to five thousand dollars and four prison years.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: What fines, jail time, and license loss apply on a first DWI or DWAI-Drug conviction versus a second offense inside ten years?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: First convictions bring five hundred to one thousand dollars and six-month loss, while ten-year repeats become four-year felonies.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: What first-offense and ten-year-repeat penalties apply to driving impaired by the combined influence of alcohol and drugs?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Mixing alcohol and any impairing drug draws the exact five-hundred-to-one-thousand misdemeanor start and ten-year felony escalation as DWI.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: Over point-zero-five through point-zero-seven, how do fines, jail days, and license actions climb across first, five-year second, and ten-year third offenses?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: First DWAI-Alcohol suspends ninety days, five-year repeats revoke six-plus months, and third offenses inside ten years turn misdemeanor.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: Compare the first-offense minimum dollar fines across DWAI-Alcohol, DWI or drug/combined offenses, and Aggravated DWI?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Mandatory court surcharges and crime-victim assistance fees stack hundreds more onto every base fine in that staircase.
sec09-card-sec09-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Three hundred, five hundred, one thousand

visual_sync.text_span: Three hundred, five hundred, one thousand

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: What rules govern mandatory ignition interlocks, driving intoxicated with a child under sixteen under Leandra's Law, and conditional licenses?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Driving intoxicated with any passenger under sixteen is an automatic felony carrying up to four prison years.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: When does DMV lifetime record review permanently deny re-licensing to a repeat alcohol or drug offender?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: DMV checks your entire driving history, blocking re-licensing after four alcohol-drug convictions or three in twenty-five years with a serious offense.
sec09-card-sec09-F09.must_match_memory_hook: Four lifetime or three plus serious

visual_sync.text_span: Four lifetime or three plus serious

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: If a driver has three alcohol-drug convictions in twenty-five years without a serious offense, what extra wait, restrictions, and interlock rules apply?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Even after serving the base revocation plus two or five extra years, returning drivers face five years of restricted interlock use.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: What criminal prison terms, suspended-driving vehicle seizures, and insurance losses hit impaired crashers beyond traffic fines?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Vehicular homicide or assault carries up to twenty-five years, while insurers can drop liability protection and leave personal lawsuits.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: What six practical steps let friends plan a night out without anyone driving under alcohol or cannabis?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Deciding how you will get home before the first drink or cannabis use removes impaired last-minute rationalizing.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: How should party hosts structure gatherings before guests leave, and which eleven core alcohol-drug topics close chapter nine?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Stopping alcohol service hours before guests depart gives time a head start while keeping sober rides front and center.
sec09-card-sec09-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Cut drinks early, know eleven rules

visual_sync.text_span: Cut drinks early, know eleven rules

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: How should you treat every railroad grade crossing, and what gear and lane rules apply while rolling across the rails?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Shifting manual gears or switching lanes mid-crossing risks stalling or catching tires right on live steel tracks.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: When is it finally legal to roll across a gated crossing, how do you approach a passive crossing, and why do train speeds fool eyes?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Large locomotives create an optical illusion that makes fast-closing trains look slower and farther away than reality.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: Contrast how a driver clears an active gated railroad crossing versus an un-gated passive crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Without flashing lights or arms, your own eyes, ears, and stop-ready approach speed become the sole safety barrier.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: What do round yellow railroad warning signs demand, and at least how many feet short of tracks must you halt for flashers, bells, or gates?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Halting at least fifteen feet back keeps your front bumper clear of lowering gate arms and locomotive overhang.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: What does a white crossbuck sign require and count, what far-side room check applies, and which three vehicle groups stop at every track?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Even empty school buses must halt at railroad tracks, so tailgating behind one invites a sudden rear-end collision.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: If your engine stalls dead on railroad tracks, what exact evacuation order, phone sign, and forty-five-degree escape angle save lives?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Running straight down the tracks away from a train puts you directly inside the flying wreckage cone upon impact.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: In exact life-saving priority order, what three steps come first when your car stalls on railroad tracks?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Never waste seconds hunting for the blue Emergency Notification System number while people are still sitting inside.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: What standard and rural speed caps apply on New York expressways, how do you handle a missed exit, and what two moves are deadly?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Backing down an off-ramp or cutting across a highway median turns a minor navigation miss into a fatal head-on hazard.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: How do you merge from a normal acceleration lane versus a short stop-controlled stub entrance, and how do right-lane drivers help?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Short parkway entrances with Stop signs lack runway to blend gradually, requiring a wide gap and brisk acceleration.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: Contrast the exact entry technique on a full expressway ramp against a short stop-signed stub entrance?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Misreading a stop-signed parkway stub like a rolling interstate ramp pushes you straight into sixty-mph traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: How far ahead must you signal an expressway exit, and why must you check your speedometer right after returning to local streets?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: After miles at highway pace, thirty-five feels like crawling without a speedometer glance to recalibrate your foot.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: What share of driving decisions rely on vision, how far ahead do headlights reach, and what bounds your safe night speed?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Outrunning your three-hundred-fifty-foot headlight cone means obstacles appear too close to halt before impact.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: During what clock window, visibility distance, and wiper condition does New York law require full headlights rather than daytime running lamps?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Daytime running lights leave your taillights dark in rain or fog, which is why law demands full headlights.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: Within how many feet must high beams drop for oncoming versus ahead traffic, and where do your eyes look if oncoming high beams blind you?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Glancing toward the right pavement edge keeps your car centered in lane instead of staring into blinding glare.
sec10-card-sec10-F11.must_match_memory_hook: Five hundred oncoming, two hundred behind

visual_sync.text_span: Five hundred oncoming, two hundred behind

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: Why are wet leaves as slick as ice, what causes hydroplaning on wet pavement, and what tire and speed habits prevent it?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Above roughly thirty-five miles per hour in standing water, worn or underinflated tires ride up on a water wedge.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: Which headlight setting cuts best through rain, fog, or falling snow, and what colors belong to legal front and rear fog lamps?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: High beams reflect straight off airborne water droplets and snowflakes back into your eyes as a blinding white wall.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: Unite New York's two footage distances for dimming high beams around traffic with the rule for rain, fog, and snow?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Remember that the two-hundred-foot following rule applies even when the vehicle ahead travels in an adjacent lane.
sec10-card-sec10-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Five hundred, two hundred, falling weather

visual_sync.text_span: Five hundred, two hundred, falling weather

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: Between which calendar dates are studded snow tires legal in New York, why never mix radial and non-radial tires, and what must clear before driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Peephole scraping leaves blind snow sheets across glass, hoods, and lamps, and AWD helps acceleration without shortening ice braking.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: How do you steer and brake out of a rear-wheel skid with ABS versus non-ABS brakes, how do front-wheel skids differ, and what freezes first?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Elevated bridges and overpasses chill from underneath as well as above, glazing over while main highways still look wet.
sec10-card-sec10-F15.must_match_memory_hook: Steer desired path, bridges freeze first

visual_sync.text_span: Steer desired path, bridges freeze first

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: Contrast your steering and transmission response in a rear-wheel skid versus a front-wheel plowing skid?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Cranking the wheel further during a front-wheel slide just plows straighter; shifting to Neutral lets side drag restore grip.
sec10-card-sec10-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Rear steers path, front waits neutral

visual_sync.text_span: Rear steers path, front waits neutral

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: Which three autumn months account for two-thirds of New York deer collisions, what daily hours peak, and why expect more than one deer?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Spotting one deer bound across asphalt almost always means trailing herd mates are about to bolt right behind.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: What habits cut deer-crash risk in signed corridors, and what is the universal first rule at the start of any driving emergency?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Taking one calm split-second before yanking the wheel prevents turning a manageable hazard into a rollover.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: How do you control the car right after a tire blowout or wheel loss, and how do you stop safely if steering fails completely?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Slamming brakes during a tire blowout or steering failure upsets balance; let momentum bleed off before gentle braking.
sec10-card-sec10-F18.must_match_memory_hook: Grip firm, ease gas, skip braking

visual_sync.text_span: Grip firm, ease gas, skip braking

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: What saves you when the brake pedal sinks, headlights black out, or the accelerator sticks — and why never turn the ignition off rolling?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: Shutting the key off at speed can lock your steering column solid and kill power-brake assist instantly.
sec10-card-sec10-F19.must_match_memory_hook: Pump brakes, shift neutral, keep ignition

visual_sync.text_span: Pump brakes, shift neutral, keep ignition

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: Contrast your foot-on-brake instinct during total brake failure versus total steering failure?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Hard braking without steering control pitches the car sideways off its straight line; coast down with flashers first.
sec10-card-sec10-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Pump dead brakes, coast dead steering

visual_sync.text_span: Pump dead brakes, coast dead steering

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: How do you recover safely when right wheels drop off pavement, and which direction must you dodge an oncoming car in your lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Swinging left into the oncoming lane turns deadly when the drifting driver wakes up and snaps back right.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: How do you handle a track stall with vs without an approaching train, and how do you escape a floating or sinking car in water?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Water pressure pins car doors shut quickly, so unbuckle immediately and climb out open windows while the car still floats.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: When a train is bearing down on your stalled car, why do you run at forty-five degrees toward the train rather than away down-track?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Shattered metal and car parts blast forward along the rails in the same direction the locomotive travels.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: What do you do if smoke pours from under your hood or your windshield view suddenly blocks, and what core emergencies close chapter ten?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Popping a smoking hood feeds oxygen straight to an engine fire; move everyone far back and let firefighters handle it.
sec10-card-sec10-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Pull off, shut engine, call fire

sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: In what two distinct ways do modern driver-assistance safety features respond when sensors spot a developing crash hazard?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Some features merely chime or buzz the wheel to wake your attention, while intervention systems actively brake or nudge steering.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: Which six everyday camera, warning, braking, steering, and parking technologies represent modern driver-assistance features?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Knowing which specific assists equip your car before pulling out keeps a surprise steering nudge or chime from startling you.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: Even when a vehicle has both hazard alerts and automatic braking or steering assists, who holds full responsibility behind the wheel?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: Assistance hardware backs up alert human eyes rather than creating a self-driving car where your attention can drift.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: Why must you study your owner's manual for ADAS limits, and which weather or road conditions can blind or confuse those systems?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: Heavy snow, fog, steep crests, and sharp curves can block radar beams or hide lane stripes right when traction drops.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: What two maintenance habits keep driver-assistance cameras, radars, and computers working reliably?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: Road salt, mud, or bumper damage over a hidden radar lens can silently blind collision warnings until cleaned or repaired.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.question_text: Why does New York prohibit parking assist and cruise control during your skills test while still requiring head checks and mirror scans?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.teaching_text: A road test measures whether you personally scan mirrors, turn your head, and modulate speed safely without automation.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: What core rule explains why cameras may stay active on the road test while self-parking and cruise control cannot?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: Glancing at a backup screen helps spot low obstacles only after you still turn your head and sweep mirrors.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: Which exact two vehicle features are completely prohibited during a New York DMV road test?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: Switch off adaptive cruise control and never activate hands-free parallel parking during your exam or the test fails.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: What standard do New York license examiners grade, and who holds the final word on your score?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: The examiner watches your eyes, hands, and pedals to verify you control the vehicle safely without relying on electronics.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: Can you still fail your New York road test while using only permitted cameras or alerts?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: Staring exclusively at a backup camera during reverse parking without turning your head fails the unassisted-driving standard.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: Which backup warnings, blind-spot systems, and camera views are allowed to remain on during your road test?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Factory backup chimes, mirror blind-spot icons, and surround-view screens stay legal as long as your physical head checks lead.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: Which five forward, speed, curve, lane, and vulnerable-user warning systems are permitted during New York road tests?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: Passive chimes for curve speed, forward collision, lane drift, and cyclist detection never steer for you, so testing allows them.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: Which two proximity and backing alerts finish New York's list of ten permitted warning systems on the road test?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: Distance beeps and rear cross-traffic chimes merely warn you of close bumpers while your own hands steer into the space.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: Why are ultrasonic parking sensors allowed on the New York road test while automatic parallel parking is banned?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: Examiners allow proximity chimes that leave you steering and braking, whereas hands-free parallel parking takes over the maneuver.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: Which four active braking, lane-keeping, or crash-avoidance assists may remain enabled during a New York road test?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Modern cars bake emergency braking and lane-keeping safety nets in by default, so New York lets those four stay active.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: How do New York's four permitted active safety assists contrast with the two banned automation features on road-test day?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: Crash-prevention nets stay legal, while convenience automation like adaptive cruise control and self-parking stays strictly off-limits.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: How do a registration and a title differ in purpose and minimum age, and how soon must new residents register?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Anyone of any age can hold an ownership title, whereas legal road registration requires age sixteen.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: What does a registration authorize versus a title certificate, and what deadline applies after moving to New York?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Permit questions love mixing ownership titles with road permission or swapping thirty days for shorter windows.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: What forms, proofs, and six-point identity items go into registering a car, what do you receive, and how do dealer and private inspections differ?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Private buyers can ask for a ten-day inspection extension, whereas dealer deliveries must already be inspected within thirty days.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: How can a registered dealership handle vehicle registration and plates on a buyer's behalf?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Paying a dealership's optional processing fee alongside state fees lets you drive off without visiting a DMV counter.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: How many insurance ID cards do New York insurers issue, what details must match your form, and where does each card go?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Even a misspelled name or single wrong VIN digit on your insurance cards stalls registration at the counter.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: Which exact ownership certificates and sale forms match new-dealer, used-dealer, out-of-state-dealer, and private-party vehicle purchases?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Notice nineteen-seventy-two and older private classics use transferable registrations instead of modern MV-nine-ninety-nine titles.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: What key form separates dealer sales from private sales, and which path still requires your own DMV visit?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: Private sellers cannot issue MV-fifty sale certificates or temporary tags, so private buyers always file MV-eighty-two themselves.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: What must you inspect on the front of a title before buying, and what happens without an official lender release?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Handing cash to a private seller while an unreleased bank lien sits on the title leaves your car open to repossession.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: Which missing disclosures or pen marks on a title cause a motor vehicle office to reject it?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Crossing out a wrong buyer name or smudging mileage numbers invalidates the entire certificate at the DMV window.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: How do model-year cutoffs govern damage and odometer disclosures on a title, and what should buyers verify on the dashboard?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Always compare the written mileage box against the actual dashboard numbers before initialing the back of the title.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: At what exact model-year age does damage disclosure end compared with odometer disclosure?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: Watch that single-year gap on test day: nine-year-old cars drop damage statements while still needing mileage.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: What mandatory inspection blocks registering or titling a Rebuilt Salvage car, and what precaution helps with out-of-state titles?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: Buying a salvaged or out-of-state bargain without checking salvage-exam rules first can leave the car unregistrable for weeks.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: How does sales-tax collection differ between dealers and private sellers, and when does form DTF-eight-zero-two need the seller's signature?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Skip the seller's signature on a below-market deal or non-family gift and DMV taxes full market value anyway.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: What happens at the DMV counter if a below-market private buyer forgets the seller's signature on DTF-eight-zero-two?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Getting DTF-eight-zero-two signed while handing over payment saves chasing down a stranger later to avoid full-value tax.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: How long do standard registrations last, how are fees set, and when can plate returns earn full or second-year refunds?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Mounting plates even briefly voids the sixty-day unused refund, leaving only a second-year refund if turned in during year one.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: Which two items must you remove from a vehicle before handing it to a buyer or trade-in lot, and why?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Leaving your metal tags or registration sticker attached routes the next driver's unpaid parking tickets straight to your name.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: When do renewal reminders mail out, which three problems block them, and does a missing reminder excuse driving expired?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Three unanswered parking tickets or an old address block your reminder notice while leaving you fully liable for expiration.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: What happens if your registration expiration date lands on a Saturday, Sunday, or state holiday?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: That automatic business-day extension works only as long as continuous liability insurance stays active across the weekend.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: How do mail renewals handle alternate shipping, full address updates, carrier changes, Utica mailings, and legal name changes?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: Writing a temporary address onto MV-eighty-two overwrites that registration file, whereas legal name changes always require an office visit.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: Which vehicles and unchanged account conditions qualify for three-step online registration renewal?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: Switching auto insurers or moving blocks the quick online credit-card path until your updated details clear first.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: If a spouse or friend renews your registration in person, whose signature and which IDs must they bring?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Even a spouse gets turned away without your own signature on MV-eighty-two plus identification for both of you.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: What key rule distinguishes renewing a registration by mail, online, or at a DMV office?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: Matching your account changes to the right channel avoids rejected envelopes or blocked online checkouts close to expiration.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: Must a registered New York vehicle keep liability coverage while sitting parked in a garage or driveway?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Parking a car for winter never pauses New York's insurance requirement unless you surrender the plates first.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: What are New York's minimum per-crash liability dollar amounts for death, bodily injury, and property damage?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: Most states skip separate death tiers, so lock in New York's fifty and one-hundred thousand death minimums alongside injury.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: What clean ratio links New York's bodily-injury minimums to its fatality minimums?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Doubling twenty-five and fifty thousand gives fifty and one hundred thousand instantly on multiple-choice liability questions.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: What happens if insurance drops before turning in car plates, when does your driver license suspend too, and which vehicle is exempt?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Letting an uninsured lapse pass ninety days without surrendering car plates suspends your personal driver license alongside registration.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: How does New York treat motorcycles differently from cars when seasonal insurance coverage ends?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: Riders must insure before riding on streets, yet seasonal winter cancellations do not require surrendering motorcycle tags.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: Who must prove valid insurance on New York roads, and what license penalty hits uninsured driving, lending, or crashing?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: Even lending your uninsured car to a friend or visiting from out of state triggers at least a one-year revocation.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: What inspection deadlines apply to New York dealer buys, private buys, and newcomers holding an out-of-state sticker?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Ask for temporary extension VS-ten-seventy-seven when registering a private buy so you have ten legal days to inspect.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: How do the thirty-day, ten-day, and up-to-one-year inspection rules match up across vehicle owners?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Test writers swap ten and thirty days between dealer lots and private driveways, so anchor each buyer type.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: Which six special transfers skip a dealer's pre-delivery retail inspection requirement?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: Buying out your own leased car skips the dealer retail-sale inspection since the car never changed drivers.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: Which two events require a fresh vehicle inspection, and what color signs mark licensed stations?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: Even six months left on an old windshield sticker resets whenever a vehicle changes registered owners.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: What does your registration-renewal signature certify about inspections, and what happens upon passing versus failing?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: Waiting until the final day of your sticker month leaves zero buffer if a rejection notice demands parts and repairs.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.question_text: What repair spend unlocks an emissions waiver, and which gas vehicles take safety-only inspections?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.teaching_text: Brand-new cars under two model years, classics twenty-six or older, historic tags, and motorcycles skip gas emissions checks.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: What roadside checks apply to any diesel in New York, and what weight rating adds diesel emissions testing?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: Out-of-state plates never shield a diesel truck from roadside safety checks while rolling across New York highways.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.question_text: What steps should you follow for a repair or dealer dispute, and what ninety-day or mileage deadline governs repair complaints?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.teaching_text: Wait past ninety days or three thousand miles—whichever hits first—and DMV's repair-shop complaint window closes.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.question_text: Which shapes and color pairs distinguish regulation, warning, destination, and motorist-service road signs?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.teaching_text: Reading background color and outline from blocks away tells you what kind of message approaches even in glare.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.question_text: What must you do at a red-and-white stop sign, and in what three-step order do you pick your exact stopping spot?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.teaching_text: Rolling past a painted stop bar or crosswalk before halting fails behind-the-wheel checks even if cross-traffic stays clear.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.question_text: How must you approach a red-and-white yield sign, and when does it turn into a full stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.teaching_text: Cruising past a yield triangle at full speed leaves zero room to halt if cross-traffic or pedestrians appear.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.question_text: How does a mandatory stop sign differ from a yield sign, including the three-part stopping-point rule?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.teaching_text: Permit traps claim empty roads let you treat an octagon like a yield triangle, which always draws a violation.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.question_text: Which six traffic rules do white rectangular regulation signs cover, and what does a red circle with a diagonal slash mean?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.teaching_text: Spotting a red circle and diagonal slash instantly signals a strict ban on whatever turn or vehicle sits underneath.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.question_text: What do yellow-and-black warning signs alert you to, and what does an attached yellow-and-black speed plaque recommend?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.teaching_text: Sharp curves and exit ramps pair diamond warnings with lower recommended speeds tuned for safe dry-road cornering.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.question_text: What do orange-and-black road signs signify, how low can work-zone limits drop, and how must you treat flaggers?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.teaching_text: Even when no temporary speed sign is posted, slowing down and following every flagger paddle protects exposed crews.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.question_text: How does the legal force of yellow warning plaques compare with orange work-zone signs and flaggers?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.teaching_text: Ignoring an orange work-zone speed sign or flagger command brings strict enforcement rather than mere curve advice.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.question_text: What information do green-and-white guide signs provide, and how do shaped route markers help navigation?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.teaching_text: Distinct shield outlines let you confirm state, United States, or interstate highways at highway speed before exit splits.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.question_text: Which four traveler needs do blue-and-white highway signs direct you toward?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.teaching_text: Keep blue motorist services separate from green exit directions when scanning highway signboards on long drives.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.question_text: In what vertical or horizontal order are traffic-signal colors arranged, and how must you treat a dark or broken signal?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.teaching_text: Colorblind drivers rely on red always sitting top or far left, while power outages turn intersections into all-way stops.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.question_text: Which two turns on steady red are normally allowed after stopping, and which signs, city rules, or school-bus rules ban them?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.teaching_text: New York City flips the statewide rule by banning turns on red everywhere unless a posted sign explicitly allows one.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.question_text: How does a flashing red light differ from a steady red arrow when you want to proceed or turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.teaching_text: Never creep right on a lit red arrow in New York because arrowed reds forbid every turn until changing.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.question_text: How do turning permissions differ across a standard steady red, a steady red arrow, and an unposted New York City red?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.teaching_text: Permit exams test all three side by side to catch drivers who assume right-on-red works on arrows or city corners.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.question_text: What distinct actions do a steady yellow circle, a flashing yellow light, and a steady yellow arrow require?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.teaching_text: Flooring the gas on a steady yellow circle or ending yellow arrow puts you mid-intersection right as cross-traffic gets green.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.question_text: How do flashing red and flashing yellow contrast, and how does a yellow arrow narrow a steady yellow's warning?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.teaching_text: Drivers crossing a flashing yellow corridor never have to stop, making full stops mandatory on the flashing-red side street.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.question_text: Does a steady green circle or green arrow give unconditional priority, or must you still yield?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.teaching_text: Pedestrians finishing a crosswalk or vehicles clearing the intersection still hold legal priority when your light turns green.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.question_text: What does each of the four reversible overhead lane-control signals—steady red X, steady yellow X, flashing yellow X, and green arrow—command?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.teaching_text: Don't confuse a steady yellow X ordering you out of a reversing lane with a flashing yellow X allowing left turns.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.question_text: What traffic rules does pavement paint enforce, when may you cross a solid edge line, and what does an inward-angling edge line warn of?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.teaching_text: Drifting over the right edge line onto the shoulder is unlawful unless a sign or officer directs you across.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.question_text: How do white and yellow lane lines differ in traffic direction, and what does a single broken line permit?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.teaching_text: Seeing yellow paint on your right means you entered a wrong-way ramp or opposing lane and must correct immediately.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.question_text: When a solid line and a broken line run side by side, what rules apply to drivers on each side?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.teaching_text: Only the line closest to your left tire governs you, allowing a driveway left turn even across the solid side.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.question_text: How do double solid lines differ from a single solid line for passing, lane changes, left turns, and obstructions?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.teaching_text: Notice New York allows crossing a single solid line around a road hazard, whereas double solids permit only left turns or U-turns.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.question_text: How do broken, paired solid-broken, single solid, and double solid lines compare on passing and crossing?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.teaching_text: Ranking all four stripe patterns together keeps you from mixing single-solid hazard detours with double-solid passing bans.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.question_text: When must you halt behind painted stop or crosswalk lines, and why are some stop lines painted far back from corners?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.teaching_text: Creeping past a set-back white stop bar blocks wide tractor-trailer turns swinging into your lane.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.question_text: Does rolling up to an empty painted stop bar or crosswalk on a green or unsigned street force a stop?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.teaching_text: Stopping randomly at an empty mid-block or green-light crosswalk surprises following drivers and invites rear-end collisions.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.question_text: What do painted pavement arrows require, and by what point must you finish picking your lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.teaching_text: Diving across a solid white turn-lane line at the last second sideswipes drivers already lined up properly.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.question_text: Which vehicles may travel in diamond-marked lanes during posted hours, and when may solo city drivers enter one?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.teaching_text: Solo city drivers may merge across broken white lines only to make an immediate right turn at the next block.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.question_text: How do human traffic directions rank against lights and signs, and which five authorized roles must you obey?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.teaching_text: When a crossing guard, flagger, fire police member, or officer waves you through red or halts green, human orders rule.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.question_text: Which two exceptions allow general cars into a diamond lane—by pavement design or by human authority?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.teaching_text: If an officer waves traffic around a crash into a bus-only diamond lane, follow that hand signal immediately.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.question_text: What behavior links a dark dead traffic light to a flashing red light, and what still outranks both?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.teaching_text: Treat every dark intersection as a full stop with right-of-way yielding unless an officer stands inside directing lanes.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: How does a license suspension differ from a revocation in New York, and can unlicensed or out-of-state drivers face both?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Revocation wipes out your existing credential completely, forcing fresh approval that DMV can still refuse.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: What violations trigger a sixty-day junior suspension, a sixty-day revocation, or a one-hundred-twenty-day suspension, and how do suspensions affect your six-month permit clock?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Any days spent suspended freeze your six-month junior-permit hold instead of counting toward road-test eligibility.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: How long does new-driver probation last for newly licensed adults, and what penalties hit first-round violations, repeats, or phone convictions?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: A single speeding or tailgating conviction during probation benches you sixty days and restarts probation.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.question_text: How does temporary suspension contrast with revocation, and how does a junior texting conviction compare with sixty-day sanctions?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.teaching_text: Picking up a phone behind the wheel doubles a junior driver's penalty on offense one.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.question_text: How does the trigger structure of junior sanctions differ from adult new-driver probation before either reaches revocation?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.teaching_text: Juniors stay under strict violation triggers throughout junior status, whereas adults clear probation after six clean months.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: What happens if you ignore a New York traffic ticket, and how are non-criminal moving tickets versus criminal charges routed in New York City?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Tossing a summons into your glovebox triggers indefinite suspension and can enter automatic guilt.
sec02-card-sec02-F04.must_match_memory_hook: Answer tickets promptly, TVB handles city

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: Where are traffic tickets heard outside New York City, and what representation right does every motorist keep?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: Whether contesting a village radar stop or county citation, bringing legal counsel remains your right.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: Which outside jurisdictions actually post moving convictions and points onto a non-commercial New York driving record?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: Routine speeding convictions from neighboring states stay off non-commercial point totals, unlike those two Canadian provinces.
sec02-card-sec02-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Only Ontario and Quebec post points

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: What happens if you ignore an out-of-state moving summons from most states, and which listed exception states stay outside that compact?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: Reciprocal compacts freeze your home license until you prove that distant court summons was resolved.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: Why is paying an out-of-state speeding ticket smart even though most states never add points to your New York record?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.teaching_text: Answering a New Jersey ticket adds zero New York points, whereas ignoring it suspends your license.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: How long does New York revoke your license after an out-of-state or Canadian alcohol, drug, or fatal driving conviction?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Serious impaired or fatal convictions follow you across borders even where ordinary moving tickets do not.
sec02-card-sec02-F08.must_match_memory_hook: Outside DWI revokes ninety, youth year

visual_sync.text_span: Outside DWI revokes ninety, youth year

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: Beyond highway vehicles, which recreational privileges face matching underage-drinking sanctions for operators under twenty-one?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Underage operators caught drinking on lakes or trails lose their boating or snowmobiling operating privileges.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: What are the minimum license sanctions for Aggravated DWI, standard DWI, alcohol DWAI, drug DWAI, and out-of-state DUI?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: Notice drug impairment revokes for six months like DWI, whereas alcohol impairment suspends ninety days.
