sec02-card-sec02-F11.question_text: How long is your license revoked for refusing a chemical test as an adult, five-year repeat offender, or driver under twenty-one?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.teaching_text: Implied-consent revocations fire administratively even if a criminal court later drops the underlying impairment charge.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: What factors scale chemical-test refusal revocations compared with alcohol and drug conviction sanctions?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.teaching_text: First-time plain DWI revokes six months, yet refusing the breath test doubles revocation to one year.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.question_text: How harshly does New York revoke drivers under twenty-one convicted of alcohol or drug offenses, including youthful-offender findings?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.teaching_text: Receiving youthful-offender court sealing never shields an under-twenty-one driver from full one-year license revocation.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.question_text: Which blood-alcohol band triggers New York's Zero Tolerance law under twenty-one, and what are the first and second sanctions?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.teaching_text: Just a single drink pushes blood alcohol into that low band and triggers administrative hearing sanctions.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.question_text: How does the six-month Zero Tolerance suspension compare with the penalty for refusing a Zero Tolerance breath test?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.teaching_text: Refusing an officer's Zero Tolerance test doubles time off the road and upgrades suspension into revocation.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.question_text: Which four speeding, school-bus, hit-and-run, or street-racing triggers bring a mandatory revocation of at least six months?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.teaching_text: Notice New York measures that three-speeding-ticket window by offense date rather than later conviction dates.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.question_text: What happens if you drive, lend, or crash an uninsured vehicle, or cancel insurance on a parked car without returning plates?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.teaching_text: Letting insurance lapse even on a broken car sitting in your driveway demands turning plates in.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.question_text: Which four reporting or financial defaults trigger an indefinite New York license suspension until resolved?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.teaching_text: Indefinite suspensions carry no calendar end date and lift only after you cure the default.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.question_text: Why does New York say preventable crash instead of accident, and can a fatal crash cost your license without a ticket?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.teaching_text: Administrative law judges review fatal collisions independently even when responding officers wrote zero roadside citations.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.question_text: What criminal penalties apply to driving while suspended or revoked, and what happens at ten or twenty unanswered-ticket suspensions?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.teaching_text: Driving while suspended is never a minor traffic infraction; officers arrest drivers and impound cars.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.question_text: How does hitting twenty ignored-ticket suspensions cross into criminal liability even when someone is not behind the wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.teaching_text: Stacking twenty scofflaw suspensions creates standalone criminal exposure regardless of whether police catch you driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.question_text: Where does New York's point table apply besides public streets, when do single offenses act alone, and what accompanies sanctions?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.teaching_text: Blowing a stop sign or texting inside a shopping-center parking lot still adds state points.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.question_text: How many points attach to child-seat faults, employer brake faults, texting or injury hit-and-run, work-zone speeding, and refusals?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.teaching_text: One cell-phone ticket drops five heavy points onto your record, nearly halfway to suspension.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.question_text: Which everyday moving violations appear on New York's point table, and how are speeding points structured?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.teaching_text: Climbing higher above the posted speed sign ratchets points steeply up toward instant suspension territory.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.question_text: How many points in what timeframe trigger suspension, how are dates measured, and what is the sole defense at a point hearing?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.teaching_text: Delaying traffic court never beats the twenty-four-month clock because DMV looks strictly at ticket dates.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.question_text: What point and insurance relief does an approved crash-prevention course grant, and what three things can it never do?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.teaching_text: Taking defensive driving with zero points on your record banks zero credit against tomorrow's tickets.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.question_text: Why can a crash-prevention course lower your point total yet fail to stop a three-speeding revocation or shrink a state assessment?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.teaching_text: Mandatory three-speeding revocations and three-year state bills ignore defensive-driving completion certificates every single time.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.question_text: What fee ends a standard fixed-term suspension, and what two charges end a Zero Tolerance suspension?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.teaching_text: Your suspension stays active past its calendar end date until you pay the termination fee.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.question_text: What is New York's standard reapplication fee after revocation, and which two situations waive that fee?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.teaching_text: Uninsured revocations skip the hundred-dollar application fee only because they carry a steep civil penalty.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.question_text: Who receives automated school-bus stop-arm camera fines, and what fine tiers apply across eighteen months as stated in the manual?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.teaching_text: Automated stop-arm cameras ticket the vehicle's registered owner whenever drivers pass flashing red bus lights.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.question_text: What civil penalties must be paid before relicensing after an uninsured revocation or a first, commercial, or repeat chemical refusal?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.teaching_text: Civil penalties stack on top of court fines and block relicensing until paid in full.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.question_text: How does the civil penalty on a one-year uninsured revocation compare with first and repeat chemical-refusal penalties?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.teaching_text: Driving without liability coverage hits your wallet just as hard as a repeat breath-test refusal.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.question_text: How much does New York's Driver Responsibility Assessment charge per year and across three years after an alcohol, drug, or refusal case?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.teaching_text: Skipping an annual responsibility installment suspends your license again even after court fines were paid.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.question_text: At what point total inside eighteen months does New York's point assessment start, what does it cost yearly, and can PIRP reduce it?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.teaching_text: Two minor tickets hitting six points inside eighteen months trigger at least three hundred dollars total.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.question_text: How do the three-year alcohol assessment and the three-year point assessment compare, and can one driver owe both?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.teaching_text: Impairment bills and violation-point bills run on independent tracks that can stack on one driver.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: How does the six-point-in-eighteen-months threshold differ in consequence from the eleven-point-in-twenty-four-months threshold?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: Confusing the eighteen-month assessment window with the twenty-four-month suspension window trips up many test takers.
